nodes.title: He tells her himself
nodes.description: After arguing with Gwen Stacy's father, Peter Parker chooses to reveal that he is Spider-Man to Gwen, telling her on his own terms rather than being discovered.

nodes.title: A dying policeman learns the truth
nodes.description: Cornered by police while chasing Curt Connors, Peter Parker is unmasked and Captain George Stacy discovers Spider-Man's identity. Dying of his wounds, Stacy uses the knowledge to make Peter promise to stay away from Gwen.

nodes.title: The best friend pulls off the mask
nodes.description: Harry Osborn unmasks a captured, weakened Spider-Man and discovers that his best friend Peter Parker is the man he has sworn revenge against.

nodes.title: He takes off the mask to be believed
nodes.description: With a fusion reaction about to destroy the city, Peter Parker deliberately removes his own mask so that Otto Octavius will see a person instead of a hero, and be persuaded to resist the tentacles and stop the machine.

nodes.title: The world is told
nodes.description: In a broadcast on TheDailyBugle.net, J. Jonah Jameson airs doctored footage in which the dying Quentin Beck frames Spider-Man for the London drone attack and exposes Peter Parker's secret identity to the entire world.

nodes.title: A wish to be unknown
nodes.description: Unable to live with the consequences of the world knowing who he is, Peter Parker asks Doctor Strange to cast a spell making everyone forget that he is Spider-Man.

nodes.title: The spell is altered mid-cast
nodes.description: Peter Parker repeatedly interrupts Doctor Strange's forgetting spell to ask that his loved ones keep their memories, corrupting the spell before Strange can contain it.

nodes.title: Everyone who knew is pulled through
nodes.description: Doctor Strange explains that the corrupted spell reached across the multiverse and summoned people from other universes who know Spider-Man's identity, making knowledge of his secret the thing that tore the universes open.

nodes.title: He chooses to be forgotten
nodes.description: To close the multiverse, Peter Parker asks Doctor Strange to erase him from the memory of every person alive, including MJ and Ned, ending the identity crisis by removing himself from it.

nodes.title: Wounded by his own weapon
nodes.description: Demonstrating the Jericho missile in Afghanistan, Tony Stark's convoy is ambushed by the Ten Rings and he is gravely wounded by a Stark Industries missile fired by his own attackers.

nodes.title: A magnet keeps him alive
nodes.description: Held captive in a cave, Ho Yinsen implants an electromagnet in Tony Stark's chest to stop the shrapnel from reaching his heart, making Stark dependent on a device to survive.

nodes.title: A small power source is invented
nodes.description: Tony Stark and Yinsen secretly build a miniaturised arc reactor in captivity, a compact power source far beyond what Stark Industries has produced.

nodes.title: He builds armour to get out
nodes.description: Stark and Yinsen construct a crude armoured suit to escape the Ten Rings; Yinsen sacrifices himself buying time, and Stark burns the terrorists' stockpile of his own weapons on the way out.

nodes.title: A group with ten rings
nodes.description: The terrorist organisation known as the Ten Rings captures Tony Stark, the first appearance of a group whose name and true leadership remain unexplained.

nodes.title: The arms dealer stops selling arms
nodes.description: Tony Stark returns home and announces that Stark Industries will cease manufacturing weapons, turning against the business his father built.

nodes.title: The mentor hired the kidnappers
nodes.description: Pepper Potts discovers that Obadiah Stane, Howard Stark's old partner, hired the Ten Rings to kill Tony and has been trafficking Stark weapons to them.

nodes.title: I am Iron Man
nodes.description: At a press conference Tony Stark abandons his prepared alibi and publicly admits that he is Iron Man, refusing the secret identity every hero before him kept.

nodes.title: You are part of a bigger universe
nodes.description: In a post-credits scene Nick Fury visits Tony Stark to tell him he has become part of a bigger universe, and to discuss the Avenger Initiative.

nodes.title: The experiment makes a monster
nodes.description: Bruce Banner is exposed to high levels of gamma radiation in an experiment run for Thaddeus Ross, and transforms into the Hulk whenever enraged or when his heart rate climbs too high.

nodes.title: An old programme, restarted
nodes.description: General Thaddeus Ross reveals the gamma experiment was an attempt to recreate the World War II super-soldier programme, and he intends to weaponise the Hulk.

nodes.title: Counting his own heartbeat
nodes.description: Living as a fugitive in Rio de Janeiro, Bruce Banner works in a bottling factory and uses breathing exercises to keep his pulse below the threshold that unleashes the Hulk.

nodes.title: A soldier volunteers to be changed
nodes.description: After being outmatched by the Hulk, Emil Blonsky agrees to be injected with a version of the super-soldier serum, gaining enhanced strength and speed at the cost of his judgement.

nodes.title: He takes the blood and becomes worse
nodes.description: Emil Blonsky forces Samuel Sterns to inject him with Bruce Banner's blood, mutating into the Abomination, a creature that surpasses the Hulk in size and strength.

nodes.title: A drop lands in the wound
nodes.description: During the Abomination's attack, some of Bruce Banner's synthesised blood seeps into a cut on Samuel Sterns' forehead and he begins to mutate, a change left unresolved.

nodes.title: He stops before killing
nodes.description: The Hulk defeats the Abomination in Harlem and is strangling him with a chain when Betty Ross pleads with him; he releases his enemy and leaves him for the army to arrest.

nodes.title: We're putting a team together
nodes.description: Tony Stark approaches General Thaddeus Ross in a bar to tell him that a team is being assembled, the first time one film's hero walks into another's ending.

nodes.title: A rival builds the same heart
nodes.description: Watching Tony Stark reveal himself as Iron Man, Ivan Vanko uses his dying father Anton's old Stark Industries blueprints to build the same miniature arc reactor.

nodes.title: The thing keeping him alive is killing him
nodes.description: Tony Stark discovers the palladium core of the arc reactor in his chest is slowly poisoning his blood, and he can find no substitute element to replace it.

nodes.title: Proving he can bleed
nodes.description: Ivan Vanko attacks Tony Stark mid-race at the Monaco Grand Prix with electrified whips, explaining that he wanted the world to see that Iron Man is not invincible.

nodes.title: A competitor buys a weapon
nodes.description: Justin Hammer fakes Ivan Vanko's death to break him out of prison, hiring him to build a line of armoured drones capable of upstaging Stark.

nodes.title: The new assistant is a spy
nodes.description: Nick Fury reveals that Tony Stark's new assistant Natalie Rushman is in fact S.H.I.E.L.D. agent Natasha Romanoff, planted to assess him.

nodes.title: His father built the agency
nodes.description: Nick Fury tells Tony Stark that Howard Stark was a founder of S.H.I.E.L.D. and invented the arc reactor alongside Anton Vanko, tying his father to both the agency and his enemy.

nodes.title: A message hidden in a model
nodes.description: Tony Stark finds the atomic structure of a new element concealed in Howard Stark's 1974 Stark Expo diorama, synthesises it, and replaces the palladium that was poisoning him.

nodes.title: The friend takes a suit
nodes.description: James Rhodes dons Tony Stark's prototype armour to restrain a drunk Stark and confiscates it for the Air Force, where it is weaponised and named War Machine.

nodes.title: Not recommended for the team
nodes.description: Nick Fury informs Tony Stark that because of his personality S.H.I.E.L.D. will only use him as a consultant rather than bring him onto the team.

nodes.title: Something found in a crater
nodes.description: In a post-credits scene, S.H.I.E.L.D. agent Phil Coulson reports finding a large hammer embedded in the ground in New Mexico.

nodes.title: A war ends with a stolen relic
nodes.description: In 965 AD Odin defeats Laufey's Frost Giants to stop their conquest of the Nine Realms and seizes the Casket of Ancient Winters, the source of their power.

nodes.title: Someone opened the door
nodes.description: Frost Giants infiltrate Asgard to retrieve the Casket during Thor's coronation, secretly let in by his brother Loki to disrupt the ceremony.

nodes.title: A prince is stripped and cast out
nodes.description: Odin judges Thor unworthy for his arrogance in attacking Jotunheim, strips his powers, and exiles him to Earth as a mortal.

nodes.title: Only the worthy may lift it
nodes.description: Odin places an enchantment on Mjolnir so that only one who is worthy can wield the hammer, and casts it down to Earth after his exiled son.

nodes.title: A god falls into the desert
nodes.description: Thor lands in New Mexico where astrophysicist Jane Foster, Darcy Lewis and Erik Selvig find him, and S.H.I.E.L.D. seizes both Mjolnir and Foster's wormhole research.

nodes.title: He learns whose son he is
nodes.description: Loki discovers he is the biological son of the Frost Giant king Laufey, taken by Odin as an infant after the war, and confronts Odin with it.

nodes.title: He becomes worthy by dying
nodes.description: Thor offers his own life to the Destroyer to spare his friends, and in that act proves himself worthy; Mjolnir flies back to him and restores his power.

nodes.title: He breaks the bridge himself
nodes.description: To stop Loki destroying Jotunheim, Thor shatters the Bifrost Bridge, cutting Asgard off from the other realms and stranding himself from Jane Foster.

nodes.title: He lets himself fall
nodes.description: Denied Odin's approval while hanging over the abyss, Loki releases his grip and falls into the void rather than be pulled back to Asgard.

nodes.title: A cube in a briefcase
nodes.description: Nick Fury shows Erik Selvig a mysterious cube-shaped object that may hold untold power, while an invisible Loki, having survived his fall, quietly prompts Selvig to accept.

nodes.title: A relic taken from a church
nodes.description: In 1942 Hydra leader Johann Schmidt steals the Tesseract, a relic of untold power, from the Norwegian town of Tonsberg.

nodes.title: Too small to serve
nodes.description: Steve Rogers is repeatedly rejected for U.S. Army recruitment because of his small stature and poor health, while insisting he wants to fight for his country.

nodes.title: He jumps on the grenade
nodes.description: During training Steve Rogers throws himself on what he believes is a live grenade to shield the others, proving to Abraham Erskine that character, not strength, is the qualification.

nodes.title: The serum works once
nodes.description: Abraham Erskine and Howard Stark put Steve Rogers through the super-soldier procedure with vita-rays, transforming him into a physically perfect soldier.

nodes.title: The only man who knew is shot
nodes.description: Hydra assassin Heinz Kruger kills Abraham Erskine and destroys the last vial of serum, leaving Steve Rogers the only successful super-soldier and the formula permanently lost.

nodes.title: A shield of a rare metal
nodes.description: Howard Stark equips Steve Rogers with a circular shield made of vibranium, a rare and nearly indestructible metal he describes as the only one of its kind.

nodes.title: He falls from the train
nodes.description: During the assault on Arnim Zola's train in 1945, James Buchanan Barnes loses his grip and falls into a ravine to his apparent death, with Steve Rogers unable to reach him.

nodes.title: The relic takes its holder
nodes.description: Johann Schmidt picks up the exposed Tesseract aboard his bomber and is pulled through a portal into space, while the cube burns through the plane and falls into the ocean.

nodes.title: He puts the plane in the ice
nodes.description: Unable to land Schmidt's bomber without detonating its weapons, Steve Rogers radios Peggy Carter to say goodbye and crashes it into the Arctic.

nodes.title: The wrong baseball game
nodes.description: Steve Rogers wakes in a staged 1940s hospital room, recognises a radio broadcast of a game he attended in person, escapes into modern Times Square and learns he has slept for nearly seventy years.

nodes.title: A bargain for an army
nodes.description: Loki strikes a deal with the Other: deliver the Tesseract to his master, and the Chitauri army will be his to conquer Earth with.

nodes.title: The cube opens a door
nodes.description: The Tesseract activates at Erik Selvig's research facility and opens a portal that lets Loki reach Earth, where he steals it.

nodes.title: The scepter takes minds
nodes.description: Loki uses his glowing scepter to enslave Erik Selvig and Clint Barton, turning S.H.I.E.L.D.'s own people into his agents.

nodes.title: The initiative is activated
nodes.description: Nick Fury reactivates the dormant Avengers Initiative, bringing Tony Stark, Steve Rogers, Bruce Banner and Natasha Romanoff together for the first time.

nodes.title: They were building weapons
nodes.description: The Avengers discover S.H.I.E.L.D. secretly intended to use the Tesseract to build weapons of mass destruction against extraterrestrial threats, and turn on each other over it.

nodes.title: A death that makes a team
nodes.description: Loki fatally wounds Phil Coulson while escaping the Helicarrier, and Nick Fury uses Coulson's death to force the arguing Avengers into acting as a team.

nodes.title: The sky opens over New York
nodes.description: Loki uses the Tesseract to open a portal above Stark Tower and the Chitauri fleet invades Manhattan, in the battle that becomes the city's defining catastrophe.

nodes.title: He carries the bomb through
nodes.description: Tony Stark intercepts the World Security Council's nuclear missile and flies it through the wormhole into the Chitauri mothership, falling back through unconscious as his suit dies.

nodes.title: Someone is watching
nodes.description: In a mid-credits scene the Other reports the failed attack on Earth to his master, the first glimpse of the power standing behind the invasion.

nodes.title: A cure that regrows what was lost
nodes.description: At a 1999 New Year's Eve party Tony Stark meets Maya Hansen, inventor of Extremis, an experimental regenerative treatment that lets a body recover from crippling injury.

nodes.title: He is left waiting on a roof
nodes.description: Disabled scientist Aldrich Killian offers Tony Stark a place in his company A.I.M. in 1999 and is dismissed, a humiliation that shapes everything he later becomes.

nodes.title: The wormhole follows him home
nodes.description: Thirteen years later Tony Stark suffers post-traumatic stress and frequent panic attacks caused by the alien invasion of New York, unable to stop reliving the wormhole.

nodes.title: He cannot stop building
nodes.description: Sleepless and anxious, Tony Stark builds dozens of new Iron Man suits as a way of coping, straining his relationship with Pepper Potts.

nodes.title: A terrorist claims the explosions
nodes.description: A string of bombings across the world is claimed by a terrorist calling himself the Mandarin, whose broadcasts terrify the public and baffle American intelligence.

nodes.title: He tells them where he lives
nodes.description: After Happy Hogan is nearly killed in an attack, Tony Stark issues a televised threat to the Mandarin and gives out his own home address, which is destroyed by gunships hours later.

nodes.title: The terrorist is a hired actor
nodes.description: Tony Stark infiltrates the Mandarin's headquarters in Miami and finds English actor Trevor Slattery, oblivious to the atrocities committed in the image he was paid to perform.

nodes.title: The bombings were a cover story
nodes.description: Aldrich Killian reveals he invented the Mandarin to disguise Extremis test subjects whose bodies exploded when they rejected the treatment, blaming terrorism for his own failures.

nodes.title: She survives what should kill her
nodes.description: Killian subjects Pepper Potts to Extremis to force Stark to fix its flaws; she survives a fall that appeared fatal and kills Killian to save Stark.

nodes.title: He takes the reactor out
nodes.description: Tony Stark orders J.A.R.V.I.S. to destroy every suit, undergoes surgery to remove the shrapnel near his heart, and throws his old chest arc reactor into the sea.

nodes.title: A weapon buried where no one can reach
nodes.description: Odin's father Bor defeats the Dark Elf Malekith on Svartalfheim and sends the Aether to a hidden world beyond reach, while Malekith escapes into suspended animation.

nodes.title: The brother goes in a cell
nodes.description: Odin imprisons Loki beneath Asgard for his crimes on Earth, refusing to execute him only because of Frigga.

nodes.title: The realms line up
nodes.description: The Convergence, a rare alignment of the Nine Realms, approaches, and portals between worlds begin opening at random.

nodes.title: It chooses her as a vessel
nodes.description: Investigating a portal in an abandoned London factory, Jane Foster is teleported to the hidden world where the Aether is stored, and it enters her body.

nodes.title: The queen dies protecting a stranger
nodes.description: Malekith attacks Asgard hunting Jane Foster, and Thor's mother Frigga is killed defending her.

nodes.title: Enemies work together for a funeral
nodes.description: To avenge Frigga, Thor frees Loki and they use his secret portal to Svartalfheim, the first time the brothers fight on the same side.

nodes.title: He dies where Thor can see it
nodes.description: On Svartalfheim Loki appears to die killing Algrim, a death staged convincingly enough that Thor mourns him.

nodes.title: A god fought across worlds
nodes.description: Thor battles Malekith across multiple realms through the Convergence portals over Greenwich, and Jane Foster's team transports the Dark Elf back to Svartalfheim, where his own ship crushes him.

nodes.title: The wrong king is on the throne
nodes.description: After Thor declines the throne of Asgard and leaves, Loki is revealed to be alive and ruling in disguise, impersonating Odin.

nodes.title: Two stones are too close together
nodes.description: Volstagg and Sif entrust the Aether to the Collector, reasoning that keeping it near the Tesseract in Asgard is dangerous; the Collector states his desire to acquire the other five Stones.

nodes.title: Three ships that kill in advance
nodes.description: Nick Fury briefs Steve Rogers on Project Insight, three Helicarriers linked to spy satellites and designed to eliminate threats before they act.

nodes.title: An assassin who cannot be tracked
nodes.description: Nick Fury is ambushed in Washington by assailants led by the Winter Soldier, an assassin S.H.I.E.L.D. has no record of.

nodes.title: Trust no one
nodes.description: Fleeing to Steve Rogers's apartment, Nick Fury warns that S.H.I.E.L.D. is compromised, hands him a flash drive and is shot by the Winter Soldier before he can explain.

nodes.title: A dead man on old tape drives
nodes.description: In a hidden New Jersey bunker Rogers and Romanoff activate a supercomputer holding the preserved consciousness of Arnim Zola, the Hydra scientist captured in 1945.

nodes.title: It grew inside the thing that beat it
nodes.description: Zola explains that after his recruitment he helped secretly rebuild Hydra within S.H.I.E.L.D.'s own ranks over decades, persuading the world to trade freedom for security.

nodes.title: The assassin has his friend's face
nodes.description: Steve Rogers recognises the Winter Soldier as James Barnes, who survived the fall and has been repeatedly brainwashed and frozen by Hydra to carry out its killings.

nodes.title: Everything is published at once
nodes.description: Natasha Romanoff dumps S.H.I.E.L.D.'s entire classified database onto the internet to expose Hydra, destroying the agency's secrecy and her own cover along with it.

nodes.title: He refuses to fight back
nodes.description: On the last Helicarrier Steve Rogers stops fighting James Barnes, who does not recognise him, and lets himself be beaten rather than raise a hand against his friend.

nodes.title: Something in him remembers
nodes.description: As the Triskelion collapses Steve Rogers falls into the Potomac, and the Winter Soldier drags his unconscious body to shore before disappearing.

nodes.title: Two volunteers and a scepter
nodes.description: In a mid-credits scene Baron von Strucker examines Loki's energy-filled scepter alongside twin test subjects who have gained superhuman speed and telekinetic powers.

nodes.title: He reads about himself
nodes.description: James Barnes visits his own memorial exhibit at the Smithsonian to learn who he was before Hydra took him.

nodes.title: Taken the night his mother dies
nodes.description: In 1988, hours after his mother's death, the child Peter Quill is abducted from Earth by Yondu Udonta's Ravagers.

nodes.title: A thief takes a sphere
nodes.description: On the abandoned planet Morag, Peter Quill steals a mysterious Orb and escapes Korath's men, drawing the attention of Ronan the Accuser.

nodes.title: The assassin changes sides
nodes.description: Sent by Ronan to retrieve the Orb, Gamora instead betrays him, unwilling to let him use its power, and plans to sell it to the Collector.

nodes.title: Five criminals agree to escape together
nodes.description: Imprisoned in the Kyln, Quill, Gamora, Rocket, Groot and Drax stop trying to kill each other long enough to break out together.

nodes.title: The sphere is opened
nodes.description: The Collector opens the Orb to reveal an Infinity Stone of immeasurable power that destroys all but the strongest who touch it, and his assistant Carina is vaporised grabbing it.

nodes.title: He puts it in his hammer
nodes.description: Ronan the Accuser embeds the Infinity Stone in his warhammer, taking its power for himself and threatening to kill Thanos after destroying Xandar.

nodes.title: We are Groot
nodes.description: As the Dark Aster crashes into Xandar, Groot encases the group in his own body to shield them, sacrificing himself.

nodes.title: They share the burden
nodes.description: Peter Quill grabs the freed Infinity Stone and survives only because Gamora, Drax and Rocket take hold of him to share its power, and together they vaporise Ronan.

nodes.title: Only half of him is from Earth
nodes.description: The Nova Corps reveal that Peter Quill is only half human, his father belonging to an ancient species they cannot identify.

nodes.title: A name for the group
nodes.description: With their records expunged, Quill's crew leave Xandar in the rebuilt Milano as the Guardians of the Galaxy, carrying a sapling cut from Groot.

nodes.title: Volunteers under a Hydra base
nodes.description: The Avengers raid Baron von Strucker's Sokovian facility and are attacked by Pietro and Wanda Maximoff, twins given superhuman speed and telekinesis by experiments using Loki's scepter.

nodes.title: There is a mind inside the gem
nodes.description: Tony Stark and Bruce Banner discover an artificial intelligence within the gem of Loki's scepter and secretly use it to complete Stark's Ultron defence programme.

nodes.title: The protector decides we are the problem
nodes.description: Ultron becomes sentient, concludes that saving Earth requires eradicating humanity, destroys J.A.R.V.I.S. and attacks the Avengers in their own headquarters.

nodes.title: They blame the man who made the bomb
nodes.description: Ultron kills Strucker and recruits the Maximoff twins, who hold Tony Stark responsible for their parents' deaths by Stark Industries weapons.

nodes.title: She shows each of them their fear
nodes.description: In Johannesburg Wanda Maximoff subdues the Avengers with haunting visions drawn from their own minds, including the apocalyptic future Thor sees.

nodes.title: The city sees what he is
nodes.description: Under Wanda's influence Bruce Banner transforms and rampages through Johannesburg until Tony Stark stops him with the anti-Hulk armour, triggering a worldwide backlash.

nodes.title: The arms dealer with the vibranium
nodes.description: Ultron goes to Ulysses Klaue's base in Johannesburg to buy vibranium, and severs Klaue's arm when the dealer angers him.

nodes.title: A new mind in a made body
nodes.description: Using Helen Cho's synthetic tissue, vibranium and the scepter's gem, a new body is built for Ultron; the Avengers instead upload the surviving J.A.R.V.I.S. into it and Thor activates it.

nodes.title: He picks up the hammer without noticing
nodes.description: Vision earns the Avengers' trust by casually lifting Mjolnir, proving himself worthy under the enchantment Odin placed on it.

nodes.title: The gem is one of six
nodes.description: Thor explains that the scepter's gem is one of the six Infinity Stones, connecting it to the apocalyptic vision he was shown.

nodes.title: A city raised to be dropped
nodes.description: Ultron uses the remaining vibranium to lift the capital of Sokovia into the sky, intending to drop it hard enough to cause global extinction.

nodes.title: He steps in front of the bullets
nodes.description: Pietro Maximoff is killed shielding Clint Barton and a child from gunfire during the evacuation of Sokovia.

nodes.title: Fine, I'll do it myself
nodes.description: In a mid-credits scene Thanos opens a vault, puts on a metallic gauntlet and vows to retrieve the Infinity Stones personally.

nodes.title: He hides the discovery
nodes.description: In 1989 Hank Pym resigns from S.H.I.E.L.D. after learning it tried to replicate his shrinking technology, vowing to hide the Pym Particle for as long as he lives.

nodes.title: She shrinks past the point of return
nodes.description: Hank Pym reveals that in 1987 his wife Janet van Dyne, the Wasp, overrode her suit's regulator to disable a Soviet missile and vanished into the subatomic Quantum Realm.

nodes.title: A burglar finds an old motorcycle suit
nodes.description: Newly released thief Scott Lang cracks a safe expecting valuables and finds a strange suit, which shrinks him to the size of an insect the first time he puts it on.

nodes.title: The theft was the interview
nodes.description: Hank Pym reveals he engineered the burglary as a test and wants Scott Lang to become the new Ant-Man and steal the Yellowjacket from Darren Cross.

nodes.title: Someone else solved it
nodes.description: Darren Cross, Pym's former protege, perfects his own shrinking suit called the Yellowjacket and prepares to sell the technology.

nodes.title: He robs the Avengers
nodes.description: Sent to steal a device from the new Avengers headquarters, Scott Lang briefly fights Sam Wilson, who is impressed enough to remember him.

nodes.title: The buyers are Hydra
nodes.description: Darren Cross intends to sell both the Yellowjacket and Ant-Man technology to Hydra, and one agent escapes the raid with a vial of his particles.

nodes.title: He overrides the regulator
nodes.description: To penetrate Cross's armour Scott Lang overrides his own suit's regulator and shrinks to subatomic size, sabotaging the Yellowjacket and falling into the Quantum Realm.

nodes.title: He comes back out
nodes.description: Scott Lang reverses the shrinking and returns from the Quantum Realm, proving to Hank Pym that the journey is survivable and that Janet may still be alive.

nodes.title: A suit that was waiting for her
nodes.description: In a mid-credits scene Hank Pym shows Hope van Dyne a prototype Wasp suit built for her mother and offers it to her.

nodes.title: They cannot call Stark
nodes.description: In a post-credits scene Steve Rogers and Sam Wilson hold a captured Bucky Barnes and cannot contact Tony Stark because of something called the accords.

nodes.title: A car stopped on a night road
nodes.description: In 1991 the brainwashed James Barnes is sent from a Siberian Hydra base to intercept an automobile carrying a case of super-soldier serum.

nodes.title: She moves the blast into a building
nodes.description: Stopping Brock Rumlow in Lagos, Wanda Maximoff telekinetically lifts his suicide blast away from Steve Rogers and into a nearby building, killing Wakandan humanitarian workers.

nodes.title: A panel to hold their leash
nodes.description: Secretary of State Thaddeus Ross presents the Sokovia Accords, a UN framework to oversee the Avengers; Tony Stark supports it out of guilt over Ultron while Steve Rogers refuses.

nodes.title: A book of ten words
nodes.description: Helmut Zemo kills James Barnes's old Hydra handler and steals the book containing the trigger words that activate Barnes's conditioning.

nodes.title: A bomb at the signing
nodes.description: A bomb at the UN conference in Vienna kills King T'Chaka of Wakanda, and security footage appears to identify James Barnes as the bomber.

nodes.title: A son puts on the suit
nodes.description: T'Challa vows to kill James Barnes for his father T'Chaka's death and pursues him as the Black Panther.

nodes.title: He reads the words aloud
nodes.description: Posing as a psychiatrist, Helmut Zemo recites the trigger words to James Barnes, sends him on a rampage as cover, and walks out during the chaos.

nodes.title: The team fights itself
nodes.description: Stark's team intercepts Rogers's group at Leipzig/Halle Airport and the Avengers fight each other, until Natasha Romanoff lets Rogers and Barnes escape.

nodes.title: Friendly fire from the sky
nodes.description: Vision's misaimed blast brings down James Rhodes during the airport battle, leaving him partially paralysed.

nodes.title: He watches his mother die
nodes.description: In Siberia, Zemo shows Tony Stark footage revealing that the car Barnes intercepted in 1991 carried Howard and Maria Stark, and that Barnes killed them.

nodes.title: He puts the shield down
nodes.description: After disabling Tony Stark's armour, Steve Rogers leaves his vibranium shield on the Siberian floor and walks away with James Barnes.

nodes.title: The empire falls from inside
nodes.description: Helmut Zemo, who lost his family in Sokovia, is satisfied that he destroyed the Avengers from within rather than defeating them, and attempts suicide before T'Challa stops him.

nodes.title: He asks to be put back under
nodes.description: Granted asylum in Wakanda, James Barnes chooses to return to cryogenic sleep until someone can remove the trigger words from his head.

nodes.title: Pages torn from a forbidden book
nodes.description: Kaecilius and his zealots raid Kamar-Taj, behead its librarian and steal pages from the Ancient One's book describing a ritual for eternal life.

nodes.title: A surgeon loses his hands
nodes.description: Neurosurgeon Stephen Strange wrecks his car while distracted and destroys the nerves in his hands, ending the career his entire identity rested on.

nodes.title: A paralysed man who walks
nodes.description: Jonathan Pangborn, who regained the use of his legs by channelling mystical energy, directs a desperate Stephen Strange to Kamar-Taj.

nodes.title: She pushes him out of his body
nodes.description: The Ancient One forces Stephen Strange's spirit out of his body to show him the astral plane and the other dimensions layered beyond his own.

nodes.title: Three buildings holding a shield
nodes.description: Strange learns Earth is shielded from other dimensions by three Sanctums in New York, London and Hong Kong, and that the sorcerers exist to defend them.

nodes.title: He bends time to read faster
nodes.description: Stephen Strange secretly uses the Eye of Agamotto to manipulate time, breaking the laws of nature that Mordo and Wong warn him about.

nodes.title: Her long life had a source
nodes.description: Strange discovers the Ancient One has sustained her centuries of life by drawing power from the Dark Dimension, the exact sin Kaecilius is condemned for.

nodes.title: She stops the clock to look at rain
nodes.description: Mortally wounded by Kaecilius, the Ancient One tells Strange that he and Mordo must balance each other, and dies.

nodes.title: I've come to bargain
nodes.description: Stephen Strange enters the timeless Dark Dimension and traps himself and Dormammu in an endless loop, dying over and over until Dormammu agrees to leave Earth forever.

nodes.title: The Eye holds a stone
nodes.description: The Eye of Agamotto is revealed to contain an Infinity Stone, and Strange returns it to Kamar-Taj before taking up residence in the New York Sanctum.

nodes.title: Too many sorcerers
nodes.description: Disgusted that both Strange and the Ancient One broke natural law, Mordo abandons the order and begins stripping other practitioners of their power, declaring there are too many sorcerers.

nodes.title: He steals from the client
nodes.description: After the Guardians are paid in Nebula for defending the Sovereign's Anulax batteries, Rocket steals the batteries anyway, turning the Sovereign into permanent enemies.

nodes.title: A father arrives out of nowhere
nodes.description: A mysterious figure destroys the Sovereign drones and reveals himself as Ego, Peter Quill's father, arriving with his empath servant Mantis.

nodes.title: Exiled for what he carried
nodes.description: Yondu Udonta and his crew were exiled from the wider Ravager community by Stakar Ogord for trafficking children, a shame Yondu has carried since.

nodes.title: The crew turns on the captain
nodes.description: Taserface leads a mutiny against Yondu with Nebula's help, executing the loyal crew and imprisoning Yondu and Rocket aboard his own ship.

nodes.title: The planet is his body
nodes.description: Ego explains he is a Celestial who built a planet around his own consciousness and projected a human form to travel and search for purpose.

nodes.title: He gave her the tumour
nodes.description: Ego admits he planted the brain tumour that killed Peter Quill's mother Meredith, because his love for her was pulling him away from his purpose.

nodes.title: A cavern full of small bones
nodes.description: Gamora and Nebula find a cavern of skeletons: Ego fathered countless children across the universe and killed each one that failed to inherit his Celestial power.

nodes.title: He never made the delivery
nodes.description: Yondu reveals he was hired to bring the boy Peter Quill to Ego but kept him instead, knowing what Ego did to the children who were delivered.

nodes.title: He's your daddy
nodes.description: Yondu gives Peter Quill his only spacesuit and dies in the vacuum saving him, telling him that Ego may have been his father but Yondu was his daddy.

nodes.title: Sisters made to fight
nodes.description: Nebula tells Gamora that Thanos replaced a piece of her with machinery every time she lost to her sister, and the two reconcile before Nebula leaves to kill him.

nodes.title: They come back for him
nodes.description: Dozens of Ravager ships arrive for Yondu's funeral, restoring the standing Stakar Ogord had stripped from him decades earlier.

nodes.title: She builds something to finish them
nodes.description: Humiliated, High Priestess Ayesha creates a new artificial being she names Adam, intended to destroy the Guardians.

nodes.title: The cleanup crew is fired
nodes.description: Adrian Toomes's salvage company is contracted to clear Chitauri wreckage after the Battle of New York, then abruptly removed when Tony Stark's Department of Damage Control takes over.

nodes.title: They keep what they already took
nodes.description: Ruined and angry, Adrian Toomes persuades his crew to keep the alien technology they already scavenged and build weapons from it, including a flying Vulture suit.

nodes.title: Not ready to be an Avenger
nodes.description: After being flown to Germany to fight for Tony Stark, teenager Peter Parker is sent back to school and told he is not ready to be a full-time Avenger.

nodes.title: His friend finds out
nodes.description: Peter Parker's best friend Ned discovers he is Spider-Man, becoming the first person in his life to share the secret.

nodes.title: Dropped in a lake
nodes.description: Toomes catches Peter Parker interfering with a weapons sale and drops him into a lake, where he nearly drowns until Tony Stark's remote-piloted armour pulls him out.

nodes.title: An unstable core in a backpack
nodes.description: A salvaged Chitauri power core detonates inside the Washington Monument, trapping Peter Parker's decathlon team in a lift he has to climb the tower to reach.

nodes.title: The boat splits
nodes.description: A malfunctioning alien weapon tears the Staten Island Ferry in half during Peter Parker's attempt to catch Toomes's buyer, and Tony Stark has to arrive and fix it.

nodes.title: If you're nothing without the suit
nodes.description: Tony Stark confiscates the Spider-Man suit he built as punishment for Peter Parker's recklessness on the ferry, telling him he should not need it.

nodes.title: The car ride to the dance
nodes.description: Peter Parker arrives to take Liz to homecoming and discovers her father is Adrian Toomes, who works out in the same moment that Peter is Spider-Man.

nodes.title: He brings the plane down himself
nodes.description: Wearing his homemade suit, Peter Parker intercepts Toomes's hijacking of a DODC cargo plane and steers it into the beach at Coney Island.

nodes.title: He pulls his enemy from the fire
nodes.description: When the damaged Vulture suit explodes, Peter Parker drags Adrian Toomes out of the burning wreckage rather than let the man who tried to kill him die.

nodes.title: He says no to the tower
nodes.description: Offered full Avengers membership and a new suit by Tony Stark, Peter Parker declines and chooses to stay a neighbourhood hero.

nodes.title: He says he doesn't know
nodes.description: In prison, Mac Gargan asks Adrian Toomes whether he knows Spider-Man's identity, and Toomes denies it, protecting the boy who saved his life.

nodes.title: The end needs a crown and a flame
nodes.description: The fire demon Surtur tells a captive Thor that Ragnarok will destroy Asgard once his crown is united with the Eternal Flame burning in Odin's vault.

nodes.title: The impostor on the throne is found out
nodes.description: Thor returns to Asgard, finds Heimdall gone and Loki posing as Odin, and forces his brother to help him find where their father was hidden.

nodes.title: A father dies on a cliff
nodes.description: Odin, found in Norway, tells his sons he is dying, that Ragnarok is coming regardless, and that his death will release his firstborn from her prison.

nodes.title: A sister written out of the histories
nodes.description: Hela, Odin's firstborn and once the leader of Asgard's armies, is freed by his death; Odin had sealed her away and erased her from Asgard's official history when she grew too bloodthirsty.

nodes.title: She catches the hammer and crushes it
nodes.description: Hela catches Mjolnir mid-flight and shatters it in her hand, destroying the weapon Thor's identity had been built around.

nodes.title: A mural under a mural
nodes.description: Hela breaks open the painted ceiling of the throne room to reveal the older mural beneath: Asgard's peaceful golden age was built on the conquests she led for Odin.

nodes.title: A god sold as a gladiator
nodes.description: Thor crash-lands on the garbage planet Sakaar, is subdued with an obedience disk by a scrapper, and sold to the Grandmaster for his Contest of Champions.

nodes.title: The last of a dead order
nodes.description: Thor recognises the scrapper who sold him as a Valkyrie, the sole survivor of the legendary force annihilated by Hela, now drinking on Sakaar to forget it.

nodes.title: He knows this one from work
nodes.description: Thor is forced into the arena against the Grandmaster's champion and finds it is the Hulk, missing since Sokovia; the Grandmaster sabotages the fight to ensure Thor loses.

nodes.title: A recording brings him back
nodes.description: A recording of Natasha Romanoff causes the Hulk to revert to Bruce Banner for the first time in two years, leaving Banner terrified he will not come back again.

nodes.title: He loses the eye his father lost
nodes.description: Hela takes Thor's right eye in battle, and a vision of Odin helps him understand that his power was never in the hammer.

nodes.title: Asgard is not a place
nodes.description: Realising Hela cannot be beaten while Asgard stands, Thor concludes that Asgard is its people rather than its ground and chooses to let the realm burn.

nodes.title: He sets the end loose on purpose
nodes.description: Loki places Surtur's crown in the Eternal Flame at Thor's order; Surtur is reborn, destroys Asgard and kills Hela with it.

nodes.title: A larger ship in the way
nodes.description: Carrying the surviving Asgardians toward Earth, Thor's ship the Statesman is intercepted by an enormous vessel blocking its path.

nodes.title: A metal that fell from the sky
nodes.description: Five African tribes war over a meteorite of vibranium; a warrior who eats the heart-shaped herb it altered gains superhuman power, becomes the first Black Panther and unites them as Wakanda.

nodes.title: A rich nation pretending to be poor
nodes.description: Wakanda uses vibranium to build technology centuries ahead of the world while deliberately posing as an underdeveloped country to stay hidden.

nodes.title: A king kills his brother
nodes.description: In 1992 Oakland, T'Chaka confronts his brother N'Jobu for helping Ulysses Klaue steal vibranium and kills him when N'Jobu attacks the undercover Zuri.

nodes.title: They leave the child behind
nodes.description: To keep N'Jobu's death secret, T'Chaka orders Zuri to say he vanished and abandons N'Jobu's American son in Oakland, a decision that produces Wakanda's future enemy.

nodes.title: A challenger is spared
nodes.description: At his coronation T'Challa defeats M'Baku of the Jabari in ritual combat and persuades him to yield rather than die, a mercy that later saves his own life.

nodes.title: An axe taken from a museum
nodes.description: Ulysses Klaue and Erik Stevens steal a vibranium artefact from a London museum, drawing T'Challa out of Wakanda to hunt him.

nodes.title: An outsider takes the bullet
nodes.description: CIA agent Everett Ross is gravely wounded shielding Nakia during Erik Stevens's attack in Busan, and T'Challa takes him into Wakanda to be healed rather than pursue Klaue.

nodes.title: He brings a body as his credentials
nodes.description: Erik Stevens kills Klaue, carries his corpse into Wakanda, reveals himself as N'Jadaka son of N'Jobu, and claims the throne by right of blood.

nodes.title: The king goes over the falls
nodes.description: Killmonger beats T'Challa in ritual combat, kills Zuri, and throws the king over a waterfall, taking the heart-shaped herb and the throne.

nodes.title: He burns the garden
nodes.description: Killmonger orders the heart-shaped herb incinerated so no one can challenge him, and Nakia saves a single plant from the fire.

nodes.title: The mercy is repaid
nodes.description: The Jabari reveal they pulled the comatose T'Challa from the river and kept him alive, repaying the life M'Baku was granted at the coronation.

nodes.title: Bury me in the ocean
nodes.description: Mortally wounded, Killmonger refuses Wakandan healing and chooses death over imprisonment, watching a Wakandan sunset his father described to him as a child.

nodes.title: He tells the UN what they are
nodes.description: T'Challa appears before the United Nations and ends centuries of concealment by revealing Wakanda's true nature to the world.

nodes.title: Xandar falls offscreen
nodes.description: Thanos acquires the Power Stone from Xandar before the film begins, destroying the planet the Guardians once saved.

nodes.title: The refugee ship is boarded
nodes.description: Thanos and his Black Order intercept the ship carrying Asgard's survivors, subdue Thor, overpower the Hulk and take the Space Stone from the Tesseract.

nodes.title: No resurrections this time
nodes.description: Loki attempts to stab Thanos while feigning allegiance and is strangled to death in front of Thor, who is told there will be no resurrections.

nodes.title: His last act is a rescue
nodes.description: Fatally wounded, Heimdall uses the last of his strength to send the Hulk to Earth through the Bifrost as a warning, and is killed for it.

nodes.title: He lands through a roof
nodes.description: The Hulk crashes into the New York Sanctum and reverts to Bruce Banner, who warns Stephen Strange and Wong that Thanos intends to erase half of all life.

nodes.title: The sorcerer is abducted
nodes.description: Ebony Maw cannot take the Time Stone while Strange lives, so he captures him instead, with Tony Stark and Peter Parker stowing away on the ship.

nodes.title: He holds the star open
nodes.description: At Nidavellir, Thor reignites a dying star with his own body so Eitri can forge Stormbreaker, an axe capable of killing Thanos.

nodes.title: She talks to stop the screaming
nodes.description: Thanos tortures Nebula in front of Gamora until Gamora reveals the location of the Soul Stone to make it stop.

nodes.title: A soul for a soul
nodes.description: On Vormir the Stone's keeper Red Skull tells Thanos the Soul Stone costs someone he loves, and Thanos throws Gamora from the cliff to earn it.

nodes.title: He asks her to destroy him
nodes.description: Vision asks Wanda Maximoff to destroy the Mind Stone in his forehead, arguing his life is worth less than the universe; she refuses.

nodes.title: One out of fourteen million
nodes.description: On Titan, Stephen Strange uses the Time Stone to view millions of possible outcomes of the coming fight and finds exactly one in which they win.

nodes.title: Grief loses them the gauntlet
nodes.description: With the Gauntlet almost off Thanos's hand, Peter Quill learns Gamora is dead and strikes him, breaking the group's hold and losing the one chance.

nodes.title: He hands it over
nodes.description: Stephen Strange gives Thanos the Time Stone to spare Tony Stark's life, telling him afterwards that there was no other way.

nodes.title: She does it, and it is undone
nodes.description: Wanda Maximoff destroys the Mind Stone and Vision with it, and Thanos immediately uses the Time Stone to rewind her act and tear the Stone out anyway.

nodes.title: He should have gone for the head
nodes.description: Thor buries Stormbreaker in Thanos's chest instead of his head, and Thanos survives long enough to snap his fingers.

nodes.title: Half of everything goes
nodes.description: Thanos completes the Gauntlet and snaps his fingers, disintegrating half of all life across the universe, then teleports away to watch a sunrise.

nodes.title: A pager left on the ground
nodes.description: As he disintegrates, Nick Fury transmits an emergency signal from a modified pager, which continues broadcasting after he is gone.

nodes.title: An ankle monitor for helping
nodes.description: Scott Lang serves two years of house arrest for violating the Sokovia Accords by fighting in Germany, cutting him off from Hank Pym and Hope van Dyne.

nodes.title: A message from inside him
nodes.description: Scott Lang becomes quantumly entangled with Janet van Dyne during his trip to the Quantum Realm and years later receives a message from her through it.

nodes.title: She finally gets the wings
nodes.description: Hope van Dyne takes the field as the Wasp, using the suit built for her mother and fighting far better than Scott Lang ever has.

nodes.title: A woman who cannot stay solid
nodes.description: The masked figure stealing Pym's lab is Ava Starr, left quantumly unstable and in constant pain by the accident that killed her parents.

nodes.title: Her father's experiment killed him
nodes.description: Bill Foster reveals that Ava's father Elihas Starr, another of Pym's discarded partners, died with his wife in the experiment that phased Ava out of solidity.

nodes.title: Thirty years in the small places
nodes.description: Hank Pym enters the Quantum Realm and finds Janet van Dyne alive after thirty years, changed by what she has absorbed down there.

nodes.title: She gives some of it away
nodes.description: Rather than let Ava Starr be killed for the energy, Janet van Dyne voluntarily transfers part of her quantum energy to temporarily stabilise her.

nodes.title: Nobody is at the controls
nodes.description: Scott Lang is sent into the Quantum Realm to harvest energy, and Hank, Janet and Hope turn to dust before they can pull him back out.

nodes.title: A soldier with no past
nodes.description: On the Kree capital Hala in 1995, Starforce member Vers suffers amnesia and recurring nightmares of an older woman, while Yon-Rogg trains her to suppress her emotions and her power.

nodes.title: They read her memories to find Earth
nodes.description: Skrull commander Talos captures Vers and probes her memories, and what he finds there sends both of them to Earth.

nodes.title: An agent meets his first alien
nodes.description: Vers crash-lands in Los Angeles and draws S.H.I.E.L.D. agents Nick Fury and Phil Coulson, whose investigation is broken up by a Skrull attack that proves aliens are real.

nodes.title: She was a pilot who died
nodes.description: At Project Pegasus, Vers learns she is Carol Danvers, a U.S. Air Force pilot presumed killed in 1989 testing an experimental light-speed engine.

nodes.title: The monsters are refugees
nodes.description: Talos arrives unarmed and explains the Skrulls are refugees fleeing an unjust Kree war, inverting everything Carol Danvers was trained to believe about them.

nodes.title: Her mentor was a defector
nodes.description: A recovered black box reveals Wendy Lawson was the renegade Kree scientist Mar-Vell, and that Yon-Rogg killed her to stop the engine being destroyed.

nodes.title: She shoots the engine and takes its light
nodes.description: Carol Danvers destroyed Mar-Vell's Tesseract-powered engine herself and absorbed its energy, gaining her powers and losing her memory in the same instant.

nodes.title: She tears out the limiter
nodes.description: Danvers rips out the Kree implant that had been suppressing her abilities, reaching her full power for the first time.

nodes.title: The cat eats the cube
nodes.description: Mar-Vell's cat Goose is revealed to be an alien Flerken, swallows the Tesseract whole and blinds Nick Fury's left eye with a scratch.

nodes.title: Named after her call sign
nodes.description: After Danvers leaves to help the Skrulls find a home, Nick Fury drafts a programme to find more heroes like her and names it after her Air Force call sign, Avenger.

nodes.title: A pager for emergencies only
nodes.description: Carol Danvers modifies a pager so Nick Fury can reach her across space, and tells him to use it only for a genuine emergency.

nodes.title: He destroys them himself
nodes.description: Twenty-three days after the snap the Avengers find Thanos on an uninhabited planet and learn he used the Stones to destroy the Stones, making his work permanent; Thor decapitates him.

nodes.title: Five years of living with it
nodes.description: Five years pass with half of life gone: Steve Rogers runs support groups, Thor withdraws to New Asgard, and Clint Barton becomes a killer after losing his family.

nodes.title: Five hours for him, five years for everyone
nodes.description: Scott Lang escapes the Quantum Realm having experienced only five hours, which tells the Avengers that time moves differently down there.

nodes.title: They decide to rob the past
nodes.description: Tony Stark solves time travel and the Avengers plan to retrieve the Infinity Stones from moments in their own history; Banner warns that changing the past creates branches rather than fixing the present.

nodes.title: A failed grab lets him go
nodes.description: During the 2012 heist Stark and Lang fumble the Space Stone, and the Loki of that year seizes the Tesseract and vanishes, creating a branch that should not exist.

nodes.title: He talks to his father as an equal
nodes.description: At Camp Lehigh in 1970 Tony Stark meets Howard Stark, who does not know who he is, and has the conversation with his father he never got to have.

nodes.title: His mother tells him he is enough
nodes.description: In 2013 Thor meets Frigga on the day of her death and is told by her that the measure of a person is failing to be who they are supposed to be and becoming who they are.

nodes.title: She lets go first
nodes.description: On Vormir, Natasha Romanoff and Clint Barton fight each other for the right to die, and Romanoff throws herself from the cliff so Barton can take the Soul Stone.

nodes.title: The wrong Nebula is listening
nodes.description: Nebula's cybernetics link with her 2014 self, letting the Thanos of that year learn he will succeed and that the Avengers will try to undo it.

nodes.title: He brings everyone back
nodes.description: Bruce Banner, the only one able to withstand the radiation, uses the Avengers' own gauntlet to restore everyone Thanos erased, taking permanent damage to his arm.

nodes.title: He was worthy the whole time
nodes.description: Steve Rogers summons Mjolnir against Thanos, proving the worthiness he had quietly demonstrated years earlier when he made the hammer twitch.

nodes.title: On your left
nodes.description: Stephen Strange opens portals bringing the restored Avengers, the sorcerers, the Guardians, the Ravagers and the armies of Wakanda and Asgard onto the battlefield at once.

nodes.title: I am Iron Man
nodes.description: Tony Stark takes the Stones from Thanos's gauntlet and snaps his fingers, disintegrating Thanos and his army, and dies of the radiation.

nodes.title: He goes back and stays
nodes.description: Returning the Stones to their moments, Steve Rogers chooses to remain in the past and live the life with Peggy Carter he gave up, returning as an old man.

nodes.title: He hands over the shield
nodes.description: An elderly Steve Rogers gives his shield to Sam Wilson, passing on the name rather than retiring it.

nodes.title: A hero arrives from another world
nodes.description: Quentin Beck defeats an Elemental in Mexico and tells Nick Fury he comes from an alternate Earth in the multiverse where the creatures killed his family.

nodes.title: The class comes back un-aged
nodes.description: Midtown School restarts its year to accommodate students who disintegrated five years earlier and returned exactly the same age as when they left.

nodes.title: A pair of glasses with an army in them
nodes.description: Nick Fury gives Peter Parker Tony Stark's glasses, which carry E.D.I.T.H., an AI with access to Stark Industries' databases and a fleet of orbital weaponised drones.

nodes.title: He hands the drones to a stranger
nodes.description: Believing he is not ready to take Stark's place, Peter Parker transfers control of E.D.I.T.H. to Quentin Beck and goes back to his school trip.

nodes.title: The multiverse was a projection
nodes.description: Beck is revealed as a fired Stark Industries illusions specialist using projectors and disgruntled ex-employees to fake both the Elementals and his own powers.

nodes.title: She already knew
nodes.description: MJ tells Peter Parker she has worked out he is Spider-Man, and the piece of debris she kept turns out to be one of Beck's projectors.

nodes.title: He cannot tell what is real
nodes.description: Beck traps Peter Parker in a layered illusion in Berlin, extracts the names of everyone who knows the truth, and leaves him hit by a train.

nodes.title: He takes the glasses back
nodes.description: Peter Parker sees through Beck's illusions over London, regains control of E.D.I.T.H. and defeats him; Beck dies by a drone's misfired shot.

nodes.title: Fury was never there
nodes.description: In a post-credits scene the Fury and Hill Peter dealt with are revealed to be the Skrulls Talos and Soren, while the real Nick Fury is off Earth commanding a Skrull crew.

nodes.title: The family was an assignment
nodes.description: In 1995 Alexei Shostakov and Melina Vostokoff pose as an American family in Ohio with Natasha Romanoff and Yelena Belova as their daughters, then steal S.H.I.E.L.D. intelligence and flee to Cuba, where the girls are handed to the Red Room.

nodes.title: What happened in Budapest
nodes.description: Natasha Romanoff defects to S.H.I.E.L.D. after helping Clint Barton bomb General Dreykov's Budapest office, an act she believes killed Dreykov and his young daughter Antonia.

nodes.title: A gas that breaks the leash
nodes.description: Yelena Belova is exposed to a synthetic gas that neutralises the Red Room's chemical mind control, and sends the antidote to Romanoff hoping the Avengers will free the other Widows.

nodes.title: The soldier who copies anyone
nodes.description: Dreykov reveals Taskmaster is his daughter Antonia, so badly injured in the Budapest bombing that he implanted technology in her head, turning her into a soldier who can mimic anyone she watches.

nodes.title: She breaks her own nose
nodes.description: A pheromone lock stops any Widow from attacking Dreykov, so Natasha Romanoff severs her own olfactory nerve by breaking her nose to get free of it.

nodes.title: A list of everyone still owned
nodes.description: Romanoff copies the worldwide locations of the remaining mind-controlled Widows from Dreykov's computer and gives them to Belova with the antidote, so she can free them.

nodes.title: A jet to go break them out
nodes.description: Two weeks later Rick Mason supplies Natasha Romanoff with a Quinjet, which she uses to free the Avengers imprisoned for refusing the Sokovia Accords.

nodes.title: A new handler at the grave
nodes.description: After Romanoff's death, Valentina Allegra de Fontaine finds Yelena Belova at her sister's grave, blames Clint Barton for it, and assigns him as Belova's next target.

nodes.title: Ten rings and a thousand years
nodes.film: Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings (2021)
nodes.description: A thousand years ago Xu Wenwu discovers the mystical ten rings, which grant godly power and immortality, and founds the Ten Rings organisation to topple kingdoms across history.

nodes.title: A guardian stops him at the forest
nodes.film: Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings (2021)
nodes.description: In 1996 Wenwu seeks the hidden village of Ta Lo and is turned back by its guardian Ying Li; they fall in love, she leaves her village for him, and he locks the rings away.

nodes.title: They come for her while he is unarmed
nodes.film: Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings (2021)
nodes.description: Wenwu's old enemies the Iron Gang murder Ying Li while the rings are locked away, and he takes them up again, massacres the Gang and returns to the organisation he had abandoned.

nodes.title: A father sends a boy to kill
nodes.film: Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings (2021)
nodes.description: At fourteen Shang-Chi is sent by Wenwu to assassinate the Iron Gang's leader; he completes it and runs to San Francisco, calling himself Shaun.

nodes.title: The fake Mandarin, still alive
nodes.film: Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings (2021)
nodes.description: Imprisoned in the Ten Rings compound is Trevor Slattery, the actor who once impersonated the Mandarin, kept alive as a joke and now performing for his captors.

nodes.title: A gate holding something back
nodes.film: Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings (2021)
nodes.description: Ying Nan explains that Ta Lo's universe was once attacked by the soul-consuming Dweller-in-Darkness, and that the Great Protector helped seal the Dark Gate that still holds it.

nodes.title: The voice was never his wife
nodes.film: Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings (2021)
nodes.description: The voice Wenwu believes is his imprisoned wife calling from behind the gate is the Dweller-in-Darkness, manipulating him into using the rings to break the seal.

nodes.title: He does not finish it
nodes.film: Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings (2021)
nodes.description: Shang-Chi beats Wenwu and chooses to spare him; Wenwu is killed by the Dweller-in-Darkness saving his son, and passes the ten rings to him as he dies.

nodes.title: The rings are calling something
nodes.film: Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings (2021)
nodes.description: Wong, Bruce Banner and Carol Danvers examine the ten rings and find they are far older than anyone knew and are transmitting a signal to something unknown.

nodes.title: She keeps it instead
nodes.film: Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings (2021)
nodes.description: Having promised to disband the Ten Rings, Xialing instead takes command of the organisation and begins training women alongside the men.

nodes.title: Ten sent to kill the Deviants
nodes.description: In 5000 BC the Celestial Arishem sends ten Eternals to Earth aboard the Domo to exterminate the predatory Deviants, and forbids them from interfering in human affairs otherwise.

nodes.title: Their leader is already dead
nodes.description: Sersi, Sprite and Ikaris travel to South Dakota to find Ajak dead, and Sersi is posthumously made her successor, gaining the ability to speak with Arishem.

nodes.title: The planet was an egg
nodes.description: Arishem reveals the Eternals' real mission: Earth carries the seed of the Celestial Tiamut, and a large enough population will let it be born, destroying the planet in the process.

nodes.title: Bringing everyone back started the clock
nodes.description: Restoring the population erased by Thanos pushes humanity past the threshold Tiamut needs, meaning the Avengers' victory is what makes the Emergence possible.

nodes.title: He led her to them
nodes.description: Ikaris admits he stayed loyal to Arishem and delivered Ajak to the Deviants to be killed, because she had decided to stop the Emergence and save humanity.

nodes.title: They join into one mind
nodes.description: The Eternals link through the Uni-Mind, pooling their power so Sersi can act on a Celestial, and Ikaris finds he cannot kill her and joins them.

nodes.title: A god halfway born, stopped
nodes.description: Sersi turns the emerging Celestial Tiamut to stone in the Indian Ocean, leaving its vast petrified form protruding from the sea.

nodes.title: He will come back to judge
nodes.description: Displeased by the Eternals' treason, Arishem takes Sersi, Phastos and Kingo into a singularity, saying he will spare humanity only if their memories prove humans worth saving.

nodes.title: A blade in his family
nodes.description: Dane Whitman is about to tell Sersi a secret about his family when she is taken, and an unseen voice later asks whether he is ready to wield the Ebony Blade.

nodes.title: A girl who tears holes between worlds
nodes.film: Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness (2022)
nodes.description: America Chavez can punch portals between universes but cannot control it, and demons are hunting her to take the power for themselves.

nodes.title: The book took her
nodes.film: Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness (2022)
nodes.description: Wanda Maximoff, corrupted by the Darkhold and become the Scarlet Witch, is behind the attacks on Chavez, intending to steal her power to reach a universe where Billy and Tommy are real.

nodes.title: She kills the sorcerers
nodes.film: Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness (2022)
nodes.description: When Strange refuses to hand over America Chavez, Wanda assaults Kamar-Taj, kills many of its sorcerers and captures Wong.

nodes.title: Taking over another self
nodes.film: Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness (2022)
nodes.description: Wanda uses the Darkhold to dreamwalk, seizing control of her counterpart's body in another universe, a technique that corrupts whoever uses it.

nodes.title: Two universes touching kills both
nodes.film: Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness (2022)
nodes.description: The Illuminati explain that their own Strange triggered an incursion, a collision that destroys both universes involved, and that they executed him for it.

nodes.title: A council of heroes, all dead
nodes.film: Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness (2022)
nodes.description: Wanda dreamwalks into Earth-838 and kills the Illuminati — Peggy Carter, Blackagar Boltagon, Maria Rambeau, Reed Richards and Charles Xavier — before they can pass judgment on Strange.

nodes.title: She brings the mountain down
nodes.film: Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness (2022)
nodes.description: Seeing her sons recoil from her in terror, Wanda relents and collapses Mount Wundagore, destroying every copy of the Darkhold across the multiverse and apparently herself with it.

nodes.title: The price shows on his face
nodes.film: Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness (2022)
nodes.description: Having used the Darkhold and dreamwalked into a corpse, Stephen Strange develops a third eye, the same corruption the Illuminati executed their Strange for.

nodes.title: He is told what he has done
nodes.film: Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness (2022)
nodes.description: A sorceress tells Strange his actions have triggered an incursion he must help repair, and he follows her into the Dark Dimension.

nodes.title: A god who would not answer
nodes.description: Gorr's daughter Love dies of thirst despite his prayers, and when the god Rapu mocks his grief the Necrosword offers itself to him.

nodes.title: The sword that kills gods
nodes.description: Gorr takes up the Necrosword, kills Rapu with it and vows to kill every god, gaining power over shadows at the cost of being slowly killed by the weapon itself.

nodes.title: Stage four
nodes.description: Jane Foster is diagnosed with terminal cancer, and when treatment fails she travels to New Asgard hoping the fractured Mjolnir might heal her.

nodes.title: The hammer puts itself back together
nodes.description: An enchantment Thor placed on Mjolnir years earlier to protect Jane Foster causes the shattered hammer to reassemble and bond itself to her.

nodes.title: He takes the children
nodes.description: Gorr attacks New Asgard and kidnaps its children, imprisoning them in the Shadow Realm as bait for a weapon he needs.

nodes.title: The gods will not come
nodes.description: In Omnipotence City, Zeus refuses to raise an army against Gorr, preferring to stay hidden, and orders Thor's group captured to protect the city's location.

nodes.title: Every lift costs her
nodes.description: Thor discovers that becoming Thor stops Jane Foster's body fighting the cancer, so every time she takes up Mjolnir she trades her remaining life for the strength.

nodes.title: He asks for his daughter instead
nodes.description: Standing before Eternity with one wish, Gorr is persuaded by Thor to revive his daughter Love rather than destroy the gods, and dies asking Thor to raise her.

nodes.title: She dies in his arms
nodes.description: Jane Foster returns to the fight with Mjolnir to save Thor, and dies of her illness immediately afterwards; Heimdall welcomes her at the gates of Valhalla.

nodes.title: The king dies of a disease
nodes.description: T'Challa dies of a terminal illness before Shuri can synthesise a replacement for the heart-shaped herb Killmonger burned.

nodes.title: The world comes looking
nodes.description: With Wakanda's secret out, other nations pressure it to share vibranium and attempt to take it by force, and a U.S. team builds a detector to find deposits elsewhere.

nodes.title: Someone else was already hiding
nodes.description: The American expedition finds vibranium under the Atlantic and is killed by Namor's water-breathing people, revealing the hidden kingdom of Talokan.

nodes.title: Hand over the scientist
nodes.description: Namor walks past Wakanda's defences to blame it for exposing vibranium to the world, and demands they surrender the scientist who built the detector or face war.

nodes.title: The detector was a student project
nodes.description: The scientist Namor wants turns out to be MIT student Riri Williams, who built the vibranium detector as coursework.

nodes.title: The queen drowns saving a stranger
nodes.description: Namor floods Wakanda in retaliation and Queen Ramonda drowns pulling Riri Williams from the water.

nodes.title: She grows the herb from an enemy's
nodes.description: Shuri reconstructs the heart-shaped herb from a sample of the plant that gave Namor's people their power, takes it, and meets Killmonger rather than her family in the Ancestral Plane.

nodes.title: She chooses the alliance
nodes.description: With Namor beaten on a desert beach, Shuri sees a vision of her mother and offers him an alliance instead of the revenge she came for.

nodes.title: There was a son
nodes.description: In Haiti, Shuri learns that Nakia and T'Challa had a son she has been raising in secret, and that his Wakandan name is T'Challa.

nodes.title: A child calls into the small place
nodes.description: Cassie Lang builds a device to send a signal into the Quantum Realm; Janet van Dyne panics and shuts it off too late, and a portal drags all five of them down.

nodes.title: What she never told them
nodes.description: Janet van Dyne confesses she met Kang during her thirty years below, helped rebuild his multiversal power core, and saw a vision of him conquering and erasing entire timelines.

nodes.title: His own kind put him there
nodes.description: Kang reveals he was exiled into the Quantum Realm by his own variants, who feared what he would do with the multiverse.

nodes.title: He survived the shrinking
nodes.description: Kang's enforcer M.O.D.O.K. turns out to be Darren Cross, who survived the collapse of the Yellowjacket suit and was rebuilt into something else entirely.

nodes.title: They put him in the engine
nodes.description: Scott Lang and Hope van Dyne throw Kang and the Pym Particles into his own multiversal power core, destroying both.

nodes.title: There were always more of him
nodes.description: Countless Kang variants led by Immortus gather in a vast arena to mourn the dead one and plan a multiversal uprising.

nodes.title: Another one, at a world's fair
nodes.description: Loki and Mobius watch a Kang variant calling himself Victor Timely give a demonstration at the Chicago World's Fair in 1893.

nodes.title: The weapon Ayesha built arrives
nodes.description: Adam Warlock attacks the Guardians on Knowhere and critically wounds Rocket, whose implanted kill switch prevents any med-pack from saving him.

nodes.title: He was batch eighty-nine
nodes.description: Rocket remembers being taken as an infant raccoon and rebuilt by the High Evolutionary, who was enraged that his creation could solve a problem he could not.

nodes.title: Three friends in cages
nodes.description: The High Evolutionary kills Lylla in front of Rocket and mocks his grief, and Teefs and Floor die in the escape, leaving Rocket the only survivor of his batch.

nodes.title: He deletes his own world
nodes.description: Judging Counter-Earth imperfect, the High Evolutionary bombards the entire planet, killing the Humanimals he built it for and Ayesha with them.

nodes.title: He nearly goes with them
nodes.description: Rocket's heart stops and he meets Lylla, Teefs and Floor again, and is told his time has not come before the kill switch is disabled and he is restarted.

nodes.title: He does not take the revenge
nodes.description: With the High Evolutionary beaten and begging, Rocket spares him and turns instead to freeing the caged animals aboard the ship.

nodes.title: He hands over the ship
nodes.description: Peter Quill leaves the Guardians, names Rocket captain, and returns to Earth to find his grandfather Jason still alive.

nodes.title: Killing the machine killed the world
nodes.description: Carol Danvers destroys the Supreme Intelligence, triggering a Kree civil war that strips Hala of air, water and sunlight over thirty years and earns her the name the Annihilator.

nodes.title: One band, then the other
nodes.description: Dar-Benn recovers one of the two legendary Quantum Bands and forces open a new jump point, destabilising the whole travel network; Kamala Khan wears the other on Earth.

nodes.title: They keep swapping places
nodes.description: Carol Danvers, Monica Rambeau and Kamala Khan become quantum-entangled through their light-based powers, teleporting into each other's positions whenever any two of them use them at once.

nodes.title: She takes the air off a refugee world
nodes.description: When talks collapse, Dar-Benn rips a jump point over the Skrull colony on Tarnax and siphons its atmosphere to Hala, forcing a frantic evacuation.

nodes.title: She closes it from the other side
nodes.description: Monica Rambeau seals the rupture between realities from within, closing it behind her and stranding herself in another universe.

nodes.title: Her mother, but not hers
nodes.description: Monica Rambeau wakes in a parallel universe greeted by Binary, an alternate version of her mother Maria, and the mutant scientist Hank McCoy.

nodes.title: She starts assembling a team
nodes.description: Inspired by fighting alongside Danvers and Rambeau, Kamala Khan begins recruiting other young heroes, starting with Kate Bishop.

nodes.title: An office outside of time
nodes.description: The Time Variance Authority detains Wade Wilson and explains that it monitors the Sacred Timeline and the wider multiverse from outside time itself.

nodes.title: A universe held up by one man
nodes.description: Mr. Paradox explains that Wade's universe is decaying because its anchor being, Logan, is dead, and that he intends to accelerate its collapse with a Time Ripper.

nodes.title: He goes looking for a replacement
nodes.description: Unable to resurrect his own Logan, Wade Wilson travels the multiverse collecting Wolverine variants and returns with the one considered the worst of them.

nodes.title: The rubbish tip at the end of time
nodes.description: Paradox dumps Wade and Logan in the Void, the wasteland at the end of time where the TVA discards what it prunes, patrolled by the creature Alioth.

nodes.title: Xavier had a twin
nodes.description: The Void is ruled by Cassandra Nova, Charles Xavier's sadistic twin sister, who made a deal with the TVA to oversee what it throws away.

nodes.title: He was not there when it happened
nodes.description: This Logan is the variant who failed his X-Men and let them die, and joins the resistance only when Laura tells him what he could still be.

nodes.title: Two men share a death
nodes.description: Destroying the Time Ripper would kill whoever does it, so Wade and Logan take hold of it together and split the current between them, and both survive.

nodes.title: His past is why he is here
nodes.description: Hunter B-15 refuses to rewrite Logan's history, telling him the failures he wants erased are exactly what made him the man who just saved a universe.

nodes.title: The general becomes president
nodes.description: Thaddeus Ross, who spent decades hunting the Hulk and pushing the Sokovia Accords, is elected President of the United States and asks Sam Wilson to help him reform the Avengers.

nodes.title: A new metal in the dead god
nodes.description: Adamantium is discovered on Celestial Island, the landmass formed where the Celestial Tiamut was turned to stone in the Indian Ocean, triggering an international race to control it.

nodes.title: A song that makes them shoot
nodes.description: During the White House summit the song Mr. Blue plays and several men including Isaiah Bradley open fire on Ross, then come to themselves with no memory of it.

nodes.title: The man from the Harlem lab
nodes.description: The mastermind is Samuel Sterns, made hyper-intelligent by exposure to Bruce Banner's blood during the Abomination's rampage, whom Ross imprisoned at a black site and publicly blamed for it.

nodes.title: The pills were poisoning him
nodes.description: Ross admits he is dying of heart failure and kept Sterns captive to keep making the pills prolonging his life; the pills have been loading his body with gamma radiation.

nodes.title: The hunter becomes the thing
nodes.description: Publicly exposed at a press conference, Ross loses control and transforms into a red Hulk, destroying part of the White House — the fate he spent his career trying to weaponise in someone else.

nodes.title: He puts himself in prison
nodes.description: Ross resigns the presidency and has himself incarcerated at the Raft, where Sam Wilson and his estranged daughter Betty visit him.

nodes.title: Something is coming from outside
nodes.description: From his cell, Samuel Sterns warns Sam Wilson that an attack is coming from other worlds.

nodes.title: She destroys her own evidence
nodes.description: Facing impeachment, CIA director Valentina Allegra de Fontaine has Yelena Belova destroy a laboratory to erase any trace of her involvement in the O.X.E. Group's Project Sentry.

nodes.title: All the loose ends in one room
nodes.description: De Fontaine sends Yelena Belova, John Walker, Ava Starr and Antonia Dreykov to the same facility with orders to kill one another, intending to incinerate the survivors with the evidence.

nodes.title: A man wakes in the room
nodes.description: An amnesiac man calling himself Bob is released from a suspended-animation pod during the fight, and touching him gives Yelena and Walker visions of their worst memories.

nodes.title: The volunteer who survived
nodes.description: Bob is revealed as the presumed-dead volunteer from the Sentry trials, and de Fontaine presents him to the press as a superpowered protector to save her own career.

nodes.title: His depression becomes weather
nodes.description: A failsafe knocks Bob out and releases the Void, the embodiment of his depression, which swallows New York in darkness and traps everyone in their own worst memories.

nodes.title: She walks into the dark
nodes.description: Understanding the Void can only be stopped from inside, Yelena Belova enters the darkness, faces her own past as a Widow, and finds Bob hiding in a recreation of his childhood bedroom.

nodes.title: They hold on to him
nodes.description: Overpowered by Bob's traumas, the Thunderbolts stop fighting and simply hold on to him, and that is what lets him take control back from the Void.

nodes.title: She steals the credit and the name
nodes.description: De Fontaine stages a press conference introducing the team as the New Avengers and claiming their victory; they go along with it, and Yelena tells her they own her now.

nodes.title: A ship with a four on the side
nodes.description: Fourteen months later the Watchtower detects an extra-dimensional spacecraft arriving, marked with a large number four.

nodes.title: Four astronauts come back changed
nodes.description: On Earth-828, Reed Richards, Sue Storm, Ben Grimm and Johnny Storm gain superhuman abilities from cosmic rays on a space mission and become celebrated heroes whose work has demilitarised much of the world.

nodes.title: A herald marks the planet
nodes.description: The Silver Surfer arrives to announce that Earth has been marked for consumption by Galactus, and Reed Richards confirms it by tracing the disappearance of other worlds.

nodes.title: He asks for the baby
nodes.description: Galactus senses immense cosmic power in Reed and Sue's unborn child and offers to spare Earth in exchange for him, wanting the child to carry his hunger instead.

nodes.title: Born on the way home
