nodes.description: Fleeing Galactus's ship and slingshotting off a neutron star, the team escapes back toward Earth and Sue gives birth to Franklin during the journey.

nodes.title: The world asks them to give him up
nodes.description: When Reed reveals what Galactus offered, public opinion turns and many demand Franklin be sacrificed to save the planet.

nodes.title: She sold her world's neighbours
nodes.description: Johnny deciphers the Silver Surfer's language and learns she is Shalla-Bal, who became Galactus's herald to spare her own planet Zenn-La at the cost of every world since.

nodes.title: They try to move the Earth
nodes.description: Reed designs teleportation bridges to transport the entire planet beyond Galactus's reach, and Sue organises the world's nations to build them.

nodes.title: She pushes a god through a door
nodes.description: Sue Storm spends all her power forcing Galactus into the portal, and dies of the effort before Franklin revives her.

nodes.title: A man with a metal mask
nodes.description: Four years later Sue returns to find Franklin at home with a man in a green cloak holding a metal mask.

nodes.title: Four years as nobody
nodes.description: Having chosen not to reintroduce himself to MJ or Ned after the spell, Peter Parker spends four years protecting New York anonymously and visiting May's grave.

nodes.title: His body changes on its own
nodes.description: After seeing MJ with someone else, Peter Parker wakes with heightened senses and organic spinnerets in his wrists, abilities he cannot control.

nodes.title: Something moving between people
nodes.description: A telepath hops from body to body attacking Damage Control facilities in search of something called V-Max, and finds it cannot enter Peter Parker's mind.

nodes.title: The telepath is a teenager
nodes.description: Peter Parker identifies the telepath as a teenage girl named Jean Grey, after she possesses MJ and nearly kills her.

nodes.title: A device that holds the other one down
nodes.description: Bruce Banner shows Peter Parker the siRNA inhibitor he uses to suppress the Hulk, and Peter builds his own to control what he is becoming.

nodes.title: She reads the letter and feels nothing
nodes.description: MJ finds the unsent letter Peter wrote to reintroduce himself; he declares his love, and she still does not remember him or feel the same.

nodes.title: The last thing her sister saw
nodes.description: V-Max turns out to be the weathered label on an air vent, the last thing Jean Grey's sister Sara saw before dying in Damage Control custody, transmitted to Jean as she died.

nodes.title: He steps in front of her
nodes.description: Peter Parker senses Frank Castle shooting at Jean Grey and shields her, taking a critical wound; Jean keeps him alive remotely with her powers.

nodes.title: The old handshake
nodes.description: Peter Parker vows to stop doing everything alone, and reintroduces himself to Ned using the handshake only the two of them ever knew.

nodes.title: A bite on a school trip
nodes.description: On a school visit to a Columbia University genetics lab, Peter Parker is bitten by a genetically engineered spider and wakes the next day with strength, agility, wall-clinging and organic webbing.

nodes.title: He tries it on himself
nodes.description: Desperate to save a military contract, Norman Osborn tests his performance-enhancing chemical on himself; it gives him superhuman strength and drives him insane.

nodes.title: The thief he let go
nodes.description: Peter Parker deliberately lets a thief escape after being cheated out of his wrestling prize, and the same man kills his uncle Ben hours later.

nodes.title: With great power
nodes.description: Peter Parker takes up the mask remembering his uncle Ben's words, that with great power comes great responsibility, and begins working as Spider-Man.

nodes.title: A cut at Thanksgiving dinner
nodes.description: At the Parkers' Thanksgiving dinner Norman Osborn notices a wound matching one he gave Spider-Man, and works out that Peter Parker is the man under the mask.

nodes.title: He is made to choose
nodes.description: The Green Goblin drops Mary Jane and a tram car full of children from the Queensboro Bridge at the same time and tells Spider-Man to pick one; he saves both.

nodes.title: His own glider kills him
nodes.description: Norman Osborn feigns remorse while triggering his glider to impale Peter Parker; Peter's spider-sense saves him and the glider kills Norman, who begs Peter not to tell Harry.

nodes.title: A son swears revenge on the wrong man
nodes.description: At his father's funeral Harry Osborn vows revenge on Spider-Man, believing him the killer, unaware that Norman was the Green Goblin.

nodes.title: He tells her they can only be friends
nodes.description: Mary Jane tells Peter Parker she loves him, and he hides his own feelings and refuses her to keep her out of reach of his enemies.

nodes.title: Something falls with the meteor
nodes.description: An extraterrestrial symbiote oozes from a fallen meteorite in Central Park and attaches itself to Peter Parker's moped while he is on a date.

nodes.title: A fugitive falls into the machine
nodes.description: Escaped convict Flint Marko, fleeing after visiting his sick daughter, falls into a particle accelerator that fuses him with sand and lets him reform his body at will.

nodes.title: The real killer, years later
nodes.description: Captain Stacy tells Peter Parker and Aunt May that Flint Marko actually killed Ben Parker, and the man Peter chased to his death was only an accomplice.

nodes.title: The suit turns black
nodes.description: The symbiote bonds to Peter Parker's costume while he sleeps, turning it black, sharpening his powers and steadily amplifying his aggression.

nodes.title: He tears it off in a bell tower
nodes.description: Realising how far the symbiote has corrupted him, Peter Parker climbs a church bell tower and uses the sound of the bell to force it off his body.

nodes.title: It finds someone angrier
nodes.description: Disgraced photographer Eddie Brock, praying for Peter Parker's death in the same church, is taken by the discarded symbiote and becomes Venom.

nodes.title: He takes the glider instead
nodes.description: Told by his butler that Spider-Man never killed Norman, Harry Osborn joins the fight and steps in front of the glider aimed at Peter, dying of the wound.

nodes.title: He forgives the man who killed Ben
nodes.description: Flint Marko explains that Ben's death was an accident and that everything since was for his daughter, and Peter Parker forgives him and lets him go.

nodes.title: His parents ran from Oscorp
nodes.description: Richard Parker records a message explaining that he and Mary fled because he refused to help Norman Osborn turn his research into biogenetic weapons; their plane is hijacked and both are killed.

nodes.title: A promise to a dead man
nodes.description: Peter Parker keeps seeing Captain Stacy's ghost and is torn by the promise he made to stay away from Gwen to keep her safe, until she ends the relationship herself.

nodes.title: He falls into the eels
nodes.description: Oscorp engineer Max Dillon falls into a tank of genetically engineered electric eels and mutates into a being of pure electricity, calling himself Electro.

nodes.title: The disease is hereditary
nodes.description: Dying, Norman Osborn tells his son Harry that the illness killing him is genetic and that Harry will begin showing symptoms soon; Harry inherits Oscorp days later.

nodes.title: He refuses to give him blood
nodes.description: Harry Osborn asks Spider-Man for his blood to cure his illness; Peter refuses, fearing what it would do to him, and Harry takes the refusal as betrayal.

nodes.title: He injects the spider venom
nodes.description: Harry Osborn forces Donald Menken to inject him with venom from Oscorp's altered spiders, which turns him goblin-like, and takes an armoured suit that heals his wounds.

nodes.title: She hits the ground
nodes.description: Having discovered Peter Parker is Spider-Man, Harry Osborn takes Gwen Stacy to the top of a clock tower; Peter catches her too late and she dies of the fall.

nodes.title: He stops for five months
nodes.description: Wracked with guilt over Gwen Stacy's death, Peter Parker gives up being Spider-Man entirely, and returns only after watching a recording of her graduation speech.

nodes.title: A life inside a sitcom
nodes.description: Three weeks after Thanos is defeated, Wanda Maximoff and Vision live an idyllic suburban life in Westview, New Jersey that moves through the decades of television history, hiding what they both are.

nodes.title: She rewinds when it slips
nodes.description: When a beekeeper climbs out of a manhole and the illusion cracks, Wanda Maximoff rewinds the whole street back to before it happened.

nodes.title: Someone says the wrong name
nodes.description: Geraldine mentions that Ultron killed Wanda's twin brother Pietro, and Wanda throws her bodily out of Westview through the barrier.

nodes.title: She comes back to a dead mother
nodes.description: Monica Rambeau returns to life in the Blip and learns that her mother Maria died of cancer during the five years she was gone.

nodes.title: A hexagon around a town
nodes.description: S.W.O.R.D. and FBI agent Jimmy Woo find a hexagonal energy field around Westview broadcasting a sitcom, with the real residents cast as characters inside it.

nodes.title: It was Agatha all along
nodes.description: The neighbour Agnes reveals herself as the witch Agatha Harkness, who has been interfering with Wanda's illusion from inside it, including planting a fake Pietro.

nodes.title: Salem, 1693
nodes.description: A coven led by Agatha Harkness's own mother tries to execute her for dark magic in 1693 Salem, and Agatha drains the life from all of them instead.

nodes.title: Grief made the whole town
nodes.description: Denied Vision's body by S.W.O.R.D., Wanda drove to the empty lot he had bought for them, and in a burst of grief manifested a house, a living Vision, and the Hex across the entire town.

nodes.title: She is given a name
nodes.description: Agatha Harkness identifies Wanda's power as chaos magic and tells her she is the Scarlet Witch, a being of prophecy she never knew she was.

nodes.title: They rebuilt the original body
nodes.description: Director Hayward reactivates the reassembled original Vision, now all white and stripped of memory, and sends it to kill Wanda's version.

nodes.title: She lets them go
nodes.description: Wanda Maximoff collapses the Hex to free Westview's residents, knowing it erases the Vision and the twins she made, and says goodbye to them as they fade.

nodes.title: She hears them calling
nodes.description: In hiding, Wanda studies the Darkhold in astral form and hears Billy and Tommy crying out to her from somewhere she cannot reach.

nodes.title: An office arrests a god
nodes.description: The Loki who escaped with the Tesseract in 2012 is seized by the Time Variance Authority, an organisation outside time that resets any deviation from the Sacred Timeline.

nodes.title: He is shown how he dies
nodes.description: In the Time Theater, Mobius shows Loki his intended future, including his part in Frigga's death and his own killing at the hands of Thanos.

nodes.title: Infinity Stones as paperweights
nodes.description: Loki gives up escaping after seeing a TVA drawer full of Infinity Stones used as desk clutter, realising the agency's power exceeds anything he has fought for.

nodes.title: The variant is another him
nodes.description: The variant killing TVA agents and hiding inside apocalypses turns out to be a female Loki named Sylvie, who wants to destroy the TVA rather than join it.

nodes.title: The staff were people once
nodes.description: Sylvie reveals that the TVA's workers are themselves variants taken from Earth and stripped of their memories, none of them knowing what they used to be.

nodes.title: The reset charges go everywhere
nodes.description: Sylvie scatters stolen reset charges across the Sacred Timeline, creating branches faster than the TVA can prune them and throwing the agency into disarray.

nodes.title: The man at the end of time
nodes.description: At the End of Time, He Who Remains explains that he pruned every branch to prevent a multiversal war between his own variants, and offers to hand the job over.

nodes.title: The machine cannot hold them
nodes.description: With the timeline branching, the Temporal Loom cannot weave the infinite new threads and overloads, spaghettifying Victor Timely and destroying the TVA.

nodes.title: He holds the branches himself
nodes.description: Rather than kill Sylvie to save the Loom, Loki destroys it, gathers the dying timelines by hand into a tree, and takes the throne at the End of Time to hold them alone forever.

nodes.title: He gives the shield to a museum
nodes.film: The Falcon and the Winter Soldier (2021)
nodes.description: Unable to see himself as Captain America, Sam Wilson hands Steve Rogers's shield to the U.S. government for a museum display rather than carry it.

nodes.title: They give it to someone else
nodes.film: The Falcon and the Winter Soldier (2021)
nodes.description: Days after Wilson donates the shield, the government announces John Walker as the new Captain America, using the symbol Wilson chose not to claim.

nodes.title: Life was better during the Blip
nodes.film: The Falcon and the Winter Soldier (2021)
nodes.description: The Flag Smashers, led by Karli Morgenthau, take a recreated Super Soldier Serum and fight to keep the borderless world that existed while half of humanity was gone.

nodes.title: There was another super soldier
nodes.film: The Falcon and the Winter Soldier (2021)
nodes.description: Bucky Barnes introduces Sam Wilson to Isaiah Bradley, a Black super soldier who fought the Winter Soldier in Korea in 1951 and was then imprisoned and experimented on for thirty years.

nodes.title: They break Zemo out on purpose
nodes.film: The Falcon and the Winter Soldier (2021)
nodes.description: Bucky Barnes engineers a prison riot to free Helmut Zemo, the man who broke the Avengers, because he is the only one who can find the serum.

nodes.title: Twenty doses in Madripoor
nodes.film: The Falcon and the Winter Soldier (2021)
nodes.description: Former Hydra scientist Wilfred Nagel, hired by the Power Broker, recreated the Super Soldier Serum and made twenty doses, which Karli Morgenthau stole.

nodes.title: He takes the vial he hid
nodes.film: The Falcon and the Winter Soldier (2021)
nodes.description: John Walker secretly keeps the last vial of serum from the batch Zemo destroys, and takes it after failing to match the Flag Smashers unaided.

nodes.title: The shield, in public, covered in blood
nodes.film: The Falcon and the Winter Soldier (2021)
nodes.description: Enraged by Lemar Hoskins's death, John Walker beats a surrendering Flag Smasher to death with Captain America's shield in a public square while bystanders film it.

nodes.title: They take it off him
nodes.film: The Falcon and the Winter Soldier (2021)
nodes.description: Sam Wilson and Bucky Barnes fight John Walker for the shield and take it back, breaking his arm; he is stripped of the title and discharged.

nodes.title: He puts on the wings and the star
nodes.film: The Falcon and the Winter Soldier (2021)
nodes.description: Sam Wilson accepts the shield and a Wakandan-built Captain America suit, choosing to carry the symbol as a Black man in full knowledge of what was done to Isaiah Bradley.

nodes.title: The fugitive was running Madripoor
nodes.film: The Falcon and the Winter Soldier (2021)
nodes.description: Sharon Carter is revealed as the Power Broker, kills Karli Morgenthau and Batroc to protect the secret, and then accepts a full pardon and returns to the CIA intending to sell its secrets.

nodes.title: Someone else picks him up
nodes.film: The Falcon and the Winter Soldier (2021)
nodes.description: Valentina Allegra de Fontaine approaches the disgraced John Walker, gives him a black uniform and renames him U.S. Agent.

nodes.title: A child watches the sky open
nodes.description: During the Battle of New York in 2012, young Kate Bishop watches Clint Barton fight the Chitauri and is inadvertently saved by him, deciding then to become a hero.

nodes.title: She puts on the wrong costume
nodes.description: At a black-market auction of items salvaged from the ruined Avengers Compound, Kate Bishop takes the Ronin suit and fights off the Tracksuit Mafia in it, making the world think Ronin has returned.

nodes.title: Ronin killed her father
nodes.description: Maya Lopez leads the Tracksuit Mafia in hunting Ronin, who killed her father William during the five years Clint Barton spent murdering criminals after the snap.

nodes.title: He admits what he did
nodes.description: Clint Barton puts the Ronin suit back on, unmasks himself in front of Maya Lopez at the shop where he killed her father, and takes responsibility for the years he spent as an assassin.

nodes.title: She comes for the man she blames
nodes.description: Yelena Belova, hired by Eleanor Bishop, hunts Clint Barton believing he is responsible for Natasha Romanoff's death, and demands the truth of it from him.

nodes.title: Maya's uncle is Kingpin
nodes.description: The figure behind the Tracksuit Mafia and Eleanor Bishop's debts is Wilson Fisk, whom Barton identifies as Kingpin.

nodes.title: He tells her how she died
nodes.description: Clint Barton tells Yelena Belova that Natasha Romanoff chose to die on Vormir to save the universe, and that he tried to go instead.

nodes.title: He wakes up two days later
nodes.description: London museum worker Steven Grant goes to sleep and wakes in the Austrian Alps at a cult meeting, then comes to at home having lost two days he cannot account for.

nodes.title: The man in the mirror is real
nodes.description: Steven Grant's reflection introduces itself as Marc Spector, an American mercenary sharing his body and serving as the avatar of the Egyptian moon god Khonshu.

nodes.title: He judges you for what you will do
nodes.description: Arthur Harrow, once Khonshu's avatar himself, now serves Ammit and intends to resurrect her so she can kill everyone who has committed or will commit evil.

nodes.title: He turns the night sky back
nodes.description: To read a two-thousand-year-old star map, Khonshu rewinds the entire night sky to the correct night, and is imprisoned in stone by the other gods for it.

nodes.title: There was a third one
nodes.description: The blackouts during which Harrow is defeated turn out to be Jake Lockley, a third alter still serving Khonshu, who kills Harrow and Ammit after Marc refuses to.

nodes.title: A bangle from her grandmother
nodes.description: Kamala Khan wears an heirloom bangle to a fan convention as part of her Captain Marvel cosplay, and it lets her project constructs of hard cosmic light.

nodes.title: They say they are exiles
nodes.description: Najma explains that she, Kamran and her group are Clandestines exiled from the Noor dimension, that Kamala's great-grandmother Aisha was one of them, and that the bangle can take them home.

nodes.title: They search her community
nodes.description: Damage Control agents hunting the enhanced girl from the convention order a sweep of the tri-state area targeting South Asian communities and raid Kamala's school.

nodes.title: A word nobody has used yet
nodes.description: Bruno tells Kamala her powers come from a genetic mutation the rest of her family does not carry, quietly naming something new in this world.

nodes.title: The bangle takes her somewhere
nodes.description: The bangle glows and Kamala Khan abruptly switches places with Carol Danvers, the hero whose costume she wore to a convention.

nodes.title: An accident with her cousin's blood
nodes.description: Lawyer Jennifer Walters is cross-contaminated with Bruce Banner's blood in a car crash caused by a Sakaaran spacecraft, and gains his powers without any of his loss of control.

nodes.title: She would rather keep her job
nodes.description: Banner trains Jennifer Walters and pushes her toward being a full-time hero; she refuses, fights him over it, and returns to practising law.

nodes.title: A law firm for the enhanced
nodes.description: Jennifer Walters is hired to head a new superhuman law division, on the condition that she work as She-Hulk full-time, turning her powers into her job description.

nodes.title: The Abomination gets parole
nodes.description: Jennifer Walters wins parole for Emil Blonsky, who demonstrates he can hold his form and mind as the Abomination, decades after trying to kill her cousin in Harlem.

nodes.title: Someone is buying her blood
nodes.description: The Wrecking Crew, armed with stolen Asgardian tools, ambush Jennifer Walters to take a sample of her blood for an anonymous client.

nodes.title: She walks out of her own show
nodes.description: Rejecting the finale she is trapped in, Jennifer Walters breaks out of the programme entirely and argues with K.E.V.I.N., the intelligence that decides what happens in this universe.

nodes.title: He comes back with a son
nodes.description: Bruce Banner returns from Sakaar bringing Skaar, a son he never mentioned, to a family barbecue.

nodes.title: The Sorcerer Supreme breaks him out
nodes.description: Wong removes Emil Blonsky from prison again and takes him to Kamar-Taj, having grown fond of the man he first borrowed as a sparring partner.

nodes.title: A promise made in 1997
nodes.description: Nick Fury recruits a million Skrull refugees, including an orphaned boy named Gravik, in exchange for a promise to find them a new home planet — a promise he never keeps.

nodes.title: They stop waiting
nodes.description: Gravik takes the Skrull Council from Talos and leads a rebellion to seize Earth by impersonating humans and provoking war between Russia and the United States.

nodes.title: He wears Fury's face to do it
nodes.description: After the Moscow bombing, Gravik disguises himself as Nick Fury and kills Maria Hill in the confusion.

nodes.title: Stolen powers in one body
nodes.description: Gravik builds a machine that splices powered DNA into Skrulls, creating Super-Skrulls able to wield the abilities of Earth's heroes, using himself as the first subject.

nodes.title: A grave full of DNA
nodes.description: Fury reveals the Harvest, a collection of DNA taken from every superhuman who fought at the Battle of Earth, hidden in a grave marked with his own name.

nodes.title: She takes the Harvest first
nodes.description: Talos's daughter G'iah uses the Harvest on herself before Gravik can, and kills him, becoming the most powerful being on Earth.

nodes.title: A law that makes everyone a suspect
nodes.description: President Ritson declares all off-world species hostile and vows to hunt the remaining Skrulls, triggering public murders of officials suspected of being aliens.

nodes.title: Someone cut the brakes
nodes.description: A staged car crash in 2007 kills Maya Lopez's mother Taloa and costs Maya her leg, sending her and her father William from Oklahoma to New York and into Wilson Fisk's orbit.

nodes.title: Her uncle set up her father
nodes.description: Maya Lopez learns that Wilson Fisk, who raised her as an uncle after her father's murder, was the informant who tipped Ronin off to kill William in the first place.

nodes.title: She shoots him in the eye
nodes.description: On learning the truth, Maya Lopez shoots Wilson Fisk in the eye and leaves New York for her hometown; he survives.

nodes.title: Her hands begin to glow
nodes.description: Maya Lopez receives visions of her Choctaw ancestors — Chafa the first Choctaw, Lowak the stickball player — and inherits a lineage of power running back through her mother's line.

nodes.title: She shows him his own childhood
nodes.description: Rather than kill Wilson Fisk, Maya Lopez uses her inherited power to take him into the memory of his father beating his mother, trying to release the anger rather than answer it.

nodes.title: He reads about the mayoral race
nodes.description: On his plane out of Oklahoma, Wilson Fisk watches a news story about a New York mayoral election with no clear front-runner, and takes an interest.

nodes.title: Three years as a detective
nodes.description: Agatha Harkness spends three years trapped in Wanda Maximoff's spell believing she is a police detective, until a teenage boy breaks into her house looking for the Witches' Road.

nodes.title: A road that grants what you want
nodes.description: Agatha assembles a coven to walk the Witches' Road, a series of trials that rewards any witch who survives with whatever she most desires — in Agatha's case, her stolen powers back.

nodes.title: The boy is Wanda's son
nodes.description: The teenager hiding behind a sigil is Billy Maximoff, the son Wanda created and lost in Westview, whose consciousness landed in another boy's body at the moment the Hex collapsed.

nodes.title: She begs Death for more time
nodes.description: Agatha Harkness bargains with Death — the witch Rio Vidal — for extra years with her son Nicholas, and spends them killing witches while he grows to despise it.

nodes.title: The song was made for a child
nodes.description: The Ballad of the Witches' Road began as a song Agatha and her son Nicholas wrote together, later used for centuries to lure witches to their deaths.

nodes.title: The Road only existed because he made it
nodes.description: Agatha admits the Witches' Road was always a con she used to rob and kill witches, and that it became real for the first time because Billy's magic made it so.

nodes.title: He goes looking for his brother
nodes.description: Billy Maximoff seals the Road, records the names of the dead, and sets out with Agatha's ghost to find his twin brother Tommy.

nodes.title: He is only supposed to watch
nodes.description: Following the shattering of the Sacred Timeline, the Watcher observes alternate branches of the multiverse where key moments went differently, sworn never to intervene in any of them.

nodes.title: She stays in the room
nodes.description: In one branch Steve Rogers is shot before the procedure and Peggy Carter takes the super-soldier serum instead, becoming Captain Carter while Rogers pilots an armoured Hydra Stomper suit.

nodes.title: The Ravagers take the wrong boy
nodes.description: Sent to Earth to collect Ego's son, the Ravagers abduct a young T'Challa from Wakanda instead of Peter Quill, and he becomes a Star-Lord who talks the galaxy out of its wars.

nodes.title: He finally intervenes
nodes.description: Facing an Ultron who has won the Infinity Stones across every universe, the Watcher breaks his oath of non-interference and assembles heroes from separate timelines as the Guardians of the Multiverse.

nodes.title: She sells her work and is thrown out
nodes.description: Riri Williams is expelled from MIT for selling coursework to other students, and takes her half-finished suit of armour home to Chicago.

nodes.title: Grief builds itself an interface
nodes.description: Mapping her own brain to build an AI for her suit, Riri Williams's unprocessed grief produces N.A.T.A.L.I.E., a digital recreation of the best friend killed in a drive-by shooting.

nodes.title: A cloak that bends the world
nodes.description: Parker Robbins leads a crew of thieves using a mysterious hood that bends bullets and reality around him, while black veins spread further across his body with every use.

nodes.title: Not the demon she assumed
nodes.description: The power behind the hood reveals himself as Mephisto, laughing that Riri Williams assumed he was Dormammu, and offers her a bargain of her own.

nodes.title: She trades for her friend back
nodes.description: Riri Williams accepts Mephisto's deal on the condition her family is left alone; Natalie is restored to life, and his veins begin spreading across Riri's arm.

nodes.title: Powered actors cannot be cast
nodes.description: Hollywood's Doorman Clause bars superpowered individuals from working as actors, forcing struggling performer Simon Williams to hide what he can do.

nodes.title: The Mandarin actor turns informant
nodes.description: Trevor Slattery, freed from the Ten Rings and rearrested, takes a deal with Damage Control to inform on Simon Williams in exchange for not finishing his sentence.

nodes.title: The apartment goes up
nodes.description: Filming a self-tape and seeing his ex-girlfriend in old footage, Simon Williams loses control and releases a blast of ionic energy inside his own apartment.

nodes.title: He breaks his friend out
nodes.description: After Slattery's arrest, Simon Williams uses a documentary as cover to get inside the Damage Control prison, and flies out with him.

nodes.title: Warriors sent out to fetch it back
nodes.description: The Hatut Zaraze are Wakandan agents sent across the world through history to recover vibranium artefacts before anyone can trace them home.

nodes.title: An agent who wanted to share it
nodes.description: In 1260 BC the rogue agent Nkati plans an independent state built with Wakandan technology, and is hunted down by Noni before he can expose the kingdom.

nodes.title: A necklace at the fall of Troy
nodes.description: Infiltrating the Greek army as Memnon during the Trojan War, a Wakandan agent lets Paris and Helen flee in exchange for a vibranium necklace, and is branded a traitor by Achilles for it.

nodes.title: The axe on display in London
nodes.description: A vibranium axe recovered by Wakandan agents ends up in a London museum, where years later Erik Stevens prepares to steal it.

nodes.title: The spider came through a portal
nodes.description: On Peter Parker's first day at Midtown High, Stephen Strange bursts out of a portal fighting a symbiotic alien, and Peter is bitten by a spider that came through with them — a bite caused by time travel rather than an accident.

nodes.title: The wrong billionaire takes him in
nodes.description: In this timeline it is Norman Osborn, not Tony Stark, who offers Peter Parker an internship and becomes his mentor and patron.

nodes.title: He saves a girl in the corridor
nodes.description: Peter Parker pulls fellow freshman Nico Minoru clear of the alien attacking their school, and the two become best friends in a life where Ned and MJ never appear.

nodes.title: He keeps what was left behind
nodes.description: After Strange and Peter send the alien back and close the gateway, a fragment of the symbiote remains on Earth and Norman Osborn quietly takes possession of it.

nodes.title: His father is in prison
nodes.description: May Parker visits Peter's father Richard, alive and incarcerated in this timeline rather than dead as in every other version of the story.

nodes.title: They kill his best friend in a bar
nodes.description: Benjamin Poindexter attacks Josie's Bar and kills Foggy Nelson, and an enraged Matt Murdock throws him from a roof before giving up the mask for a year.

nodes.title: The crime boss wins the election
nodes.description: Wilson Fisk runs for mayor of New York on an anti-vigilante platform and wins, turning the city's government into an instrument against people like Murdock.

nodes.title: Two men agree on terms
nodes.description: Murdock and Fisk meet as lawyer and candidate and each promises consequences if the other returns to what he was, a truce neither of them can keep.

nodes.title: A vigilante on trial for murder
nodes.description: Matt Murdock defends Hector Ayala, secretly the vigilante White Tiger, after two off-duty police officers frame him for a death in a subway station.

nodes.title: He declares martial law
nodes.description: Having consolidated power, Fisk declares martial law and forms an Anti-Vigilante Task Force to hunt masked people through the city.

nodes.title: He takes the deal and leaves
nodes.description: Cornered after killing protesters, Wilson Fisk is talked by Murdock into accepting exile from New York, and the Task Force is disbanded and arrested.

nodes.title: The lawyer goes to prison
nodes.description: With Fisk gone and the city recovering, Matt Murdock is arrested and imprisoned for everything he did as Daredevil.

nodes.title: A virus takes the Avengers
nodes.description: In a branch of the multiverse a virus turns most of Earth's population, the Avengers included, into zombies, and the survivors scavenge a ruined world five years later.

nodes.title: A device inside a corpse
nodes.description: Kamala Khan, Kate Bishop and Riri Williams find a shrunken transmitter inside a zombified Erik Selvig, which must be broadcast from space to call the Nova Corps.

nodes.title: A father passes the rings to hold back the bite
nodes.description: When Shang-Chi is bitten, Xu Wenwu gives him the ten rings to contain the infection and sacrifices himself covering the group's escape.

nodes.title: The Queen of the Dead
nodes.description: The zombie hordes are commanded by Wanda Maximoff, the Queen of the Dead, who wants the Infinity Stones' energy to remake the world in her own image.

nodes.title: She agrees to remake it
nodes.description: With nearly everyone dead, Kamala Khan is persuaded to help Wanda remake the world, and wakes in a restored life that flickers when the real Riri tells her none of it is true.

nodes.title: He did not stay dead
nodes.description: Phil Coulson, killed by Loki before the Battle of New York, is revealed to have survived and assembles a small team to investigate superhumans now that they are public knowledge.

nodes.title: Extremis in a cheaper package
nodes.description: Coulson's team investigates Project Centipede, which supplies an Extremis-based serum to ordinary people, some of whom explode when their bodies reject it.

nodes.title: The agency turns inside out
nodes.description: Hydra's presence inside S.H.I.E.L.D. is exposed and the organisation collapses; Grant Ward is revealed as a Hydra agent embedded in Coulson's own team.

nodes.title: He rebuilds it from nothing
nodes.description: With S.H.I.E.L.D. destroyed and outlawed, Coulson is made director and rebuilds the agency in secret while fighting Hydra and a faction of anti-superhuman former agents.

nodes.title: A hidden race in the bloodline
nodes.description: Exposure to Terrigen reveals the Inhumans, people carrying dormant alien genetics that transform them, including Coulson's own agent Daisy Johnson.

nodes.title: A team of the transformed
nodes.description: Coulson secretly assembles the Secret Warriors from Inhumans, while Hydra works to restore its ancient Inhuman founder Hive to power.

nodes.title: The Accords make them legal again
nodes.description: After Hive and Hydra are defeated, the signing of the Sokovia Accords restores S.H.I.E.L.D. as a legitimate organisation, and Coulson steps back to field work so it can have a public face.

nodes.title: A burning skull in a muscle car
nodes.description: S.H.I.E.L.D. encounters Robbie Reyes, the Ghost Rider, whose supernatural bargain later proves fatal to Coulson through their contact.

nodes.title: A world built for the guilty
nodes.description: Leo Fitz and Holden Radcliffe complete Life Model Decoys and the Framework, a virtual world where each person's greatest regret has been undone, and the team is trapped inside their own rewritten lives.

nodes.title: Taken to the end of the world
nodes.description: The team is abducted to the space station Lighthouse in 2091, where Earth has been shattered and the remnants of humanity live under alien rule, and they return determined to prevent it.

nodes.title: The bargain comes due
nodes.description: Having prevented the future they were shown, Phil Coulson dies of the damage done by his contact with the Ghost Rider, refusing any further cure.

nodes.title: A copy of a dead man
nodes.description: The team continues with a Life Model Decoy of Coulson, a machine carrying his memories that must decide what it owes to a man it is not.

nodes.title: They try to delete the agency from history
nodes.description: The Chronicoms jump through time to erase S.H.I.E.L.D. from history and claim Earth as their new homeworld, forcing the team to defend their own past.

nodes.title: They give the machines empathy
nodes.description: Melinda May and Kora combine their abilities to give the Chronicoms empathy, ending the assault without destroying them.

nodes.title: Filing paperwork after the war
nodes.description: In 1946 Peggy Carter, mourning Steve Rogers, is relegated to routine office work at the Strategic Scientific Reserve while the men she outranks in ability treat her as a secretary.

nodes.title: Howard Stark is framed
nodes.description: Howard Stark is accused of selling weapons to America's enemies and secretly asks Peggy Carter to clear his name, lending her his butler Edwin Jarvis.

nodes.title: A scientist called Vanko
nodes.description: Peggy Carter brings a stolen nitramene bomb to Stark Industries scientist Anton Vanko, who traces it to a Roxxon refinery.

nodes.title: An organisation called Leviathan
nodes.description: Carter's investigation leads to Leviathan, a Soviet organisation running agents inside American industry, and to the Red Room programme that trained them as children.

nodes.title: Nine men who own the country
nodes.description: In Los Angeles Carter uncovers the Council of Nine, a cabal of industrialists and officials steering American policy from behind it.

nodes.title: Something from another dimension
nodes.description: Scientist Whitney Frost is exposed to Zero Matter, a substance from another dimension that consumes what it touches and gradually takes her mind.

nodes.title: She chooses to stay
nodes.description: With Frost contained, Peggy Carter is persuaded to stay in Los Angeles with Daniel Sousa rather than return to New York, and Jack Thompson is shot for a file bearing her name.

nodes.title: The neighbourhood the aliens wrecked
nodes.description: Crime cartels move into Hell's Kitchen to exploit the rebuilding after the alien attack on New York, which everyone in the city refers to only as the incident.

nodes.title: Chemicals in his eyes
nodes.description: Blinded as a child in an accident that sharpened every other sense past human limits, Matt Murdock practises law by day and fights the city's criminals at night.

nodes.title: His father won the fight he was told to lose
nodes.description: Matt Murdock's father was murdered by the Irish mob for refusing to throw a fight, the first lesson his son learned about what standing up costs.

nodes.title: A nurse pulls him from a dumpster
nodes.description: Nurse Claire Temple finds a beaten Matt Murdock in a dumpster and patches him up, becoming the medic several of the city's vigilantes quietly rely on.

nodes.title: A man rebuilding a city his way
nodes.description: Wilson Fisk unites the Russian, Yakuza and Chinese operations under himself while presenting publicly as a philanthropist rebuilding Hell's Kitchen.

nodes.title: A vigilante who kills
nodes.description: Matt Murdock crosses paths with Frank Castle, a vigilante who solves the same problem by killing, forcing Murdock to defend a line he cannot fully justify.

nodes.title: He beats him and stops
nodes.description: Matt Murdock overpowers Wilson Fisk in his own penthouse and refuses to kill him, trading his silence about Vanessa for Fisk returning to prison and leaving his friends alone.

nodes.title: A voice she could not refuse
nodes.description: Jessica Jones's brief career as a hero ended when Kilgrave, who can make anyone obey a spoken command, controlled her and made her kill someone.

nodes.title: He is not dead after all
nodes.description: Believing Kilgrave died under a bus, Jessica Jones discovers he survived and is controlling a young woman named Hope, and makes Hope murder her own parents in front of her.

nodes.title: Two unbreakable people
nodes.description: Jessica Jones sleeps with bar owner Luke Cage while investigating him, and discovers his skin cannot be cut — the first of them to find another like themselves.

nodes.title: Her sister goes further than she does
nodes.description: Trish Walker acquires powers of her own and becomes a masked vigilante who starts killing, until Jessica Jones exposes her identity and sends her to the Raft.

nodes.title: A sabotaged experiment in prison
nodes.description: An experiment sabotaged while Luke Cage was in prison gives him enormous strength and skin that cannot be broken, and he escapes to Harlem as a fugitive.

nodes.title: Hammer Industries guns on the street
nodes.description: Cornell Stokes traffics Hammer Industries weapons through Harlem, salvaged technology from a defunct arms company leaking down to street gangs.

nodes.title: They shoot up the barbershop
nodes.description: Henry Hunter's barbershop, the neutral ground of the neighbourhood, is shot up and Pop is killed, which is what makes Luke Cage stop hiding.

nodes.title: A bulletproof man in a hoodie
nodes.description: Luke Cage stops hiding and becomes a public figure in Harlem, a Black man walking through gunfire in a hooded sweatshirt while the neighbourhood watches.

nodes.title: He inherits the room he washed dishes in
nodes.description: Mariah Dillard leaves Harlem's Paradise to Luke Cage in her will, and he takes it, establishing himself as the neighbourhood's law and worrying everyone who knows him.

nodes.title: A dead heir walks in barefoot
nodes.description: Presumed dead for fifteen years after a Himalayan plane crash, Danny Rand walks into Rand Enterprises to reclaim his family's company and nobody believes he is who he says.

nodes.title: The dead partner is alive upstairs
nodes.description: Harold Meachum faked his own death and has been running Rand Enterprises from hiding, kept alive by the Hand in exchange for his obedience.

nodes.title: He came back with a weapon in his hand
nodes.description: Danny Rand survived the crash and was raised in the hidden city of K'un-Lun, where he became the Iron Fist, sworn enemy of the Hand and guardian of a gate he abandoned to come home.

nodes.title: She takes the power instead
nodes.description: Colleen Wing takes on the Iron Fist power and the duty of protecting Chinatown, while Danny Rand leaves New York to look for the man Davos took it from.

nodes.title: Four strangers in the same building
nodes.description: Matt Murdock, Jessica Jones, Luke Cage and Danny Rand converge on the Hand's operation in New York, four people who have each been fighting the same organisation without knowing it.

nodes.title: They are digging under the city
nodes.description: The Hand's excavation beneath New York triggers an earthquake felt across the city, uncovering the substance their leaders need to keep living.

nodes.title: They brought her back wrong
nodes.description: Elektra Natchios is resurrected by the Hand as their Black Sky, a weapon with no memory of Matt Murdock until he reaches her at the end.

nodes.title: He stays in the building
nodes.description: Matt Murdock stays behind to plead with Elektra as the Hand's cavern implodes; the others believe him dead, and he wakes months later in a room with a nun beside him.

nodes.title: His family died in a park
nodes.description: Marine veteran Frank Castle hunts down and kills the last of the men responsible for his family's deaths, and then has nothing left to do with himself.

nodes.title: What happened in Kandahar
nodes.description: Castle's family was killed to bury what his unit did in Kandahar, a conspiracy reaching into Homeland Security and the CIA rather than the gang violence it was staged as.

nodes.title: A dead analyst watching the cameras
nodes.description: David Lieberman, an NSA analyst who faked his death to protect his family, tracks Frank Castle through the city's cameras and forces an alliance on him.

nodes.title: He stops pretending to want out
nodes.description: After a stretch of quiet life on the road, Frank Castle accepts what he is, takes up the Punisher name permanently and turns down a legitimate job offer.

nodes.title: A hidden city on the moon
nodes.description: The Inhuman Royal Family rule Attilan, a hidden city on the far side of the Moon, where every citizen's place is decided by what Terrigenesis turns them into.

nodes.title: A king who cannot speak
nodes.description: Black Bolt's voice is destructive enough to level buildings, so he rules in silence, and killed his own parents with it as a boy.

nodes.title: His brother takes the throne
nodes.description: Maximus, who emerged from Terrigenesis with no powers and no standing, stages a military coup against Black Bolt and scatters the Royal Family to Hawaii.

nodes.title: They leave the city to die
nodes.description: With Attilan failing, the Royal Family evacuate every Inhuman to Earth, lock Maximus inside the empty city, and leave it to collapse behind them.

nodes.title: Their parents are killing people
nodes.description: Six teenagers drift back together and find a hidden passage in one of their houses, where they watch their own parents sacrifice a girl in a ritual.

nodes.title: Each of them finds something
nodes.description: Karolina Dean's hands begin to glow, Molly Hernandez discovers superhuman strength, Nico Minoru inherits a staff of magic, and Gert Yorkes finds a genetically engineered dinosaur bonded to her mind.

nodes.title: A church built around one of them
nodes.description: The Church of Gibborim recruits vulnerable young people for the Pride's rituals, and is run by Leslie Dean on behalf of an alien her family has served for generations.

nodes.title: They leave and do not come back
nodes.description: Unable to trust any adult they know, the six teenagers run from their own families and live rough while trying to dismantle the Pride.

nodes.title: Magic older than any of them
nodes.description: Nico Minoru's staff draws the attention of Morgan le Fay, an ancient sorceress who fights the group across the Dark Dimension and their own timeline.

nodes.title: A note from a future that failed
nodes.description: After erasing a future in which they lose, Alex Wilder finds a note left from it naming Mancha and instructing him to kill Nico, and quietly puts it in his pocket.

nodes.title: A rig blows and two lives change
nodes.description: The Roxxon Gulf platform explodes off New Orleans; Tandy Bowen's father dies in the crash into the water and Tyrone Johnson's brother is shot by a policeman, and both children are altered by energy from the rig.

nodes.title: They touch and it switches on
nodes.description: Eight years later Tandy Bowen and Tyrone Johnson collide at a party and the contact activates their powers — she forms daggers of light, he can teleport through darkness.

nodes.title: They only work properly together
nodes.description: Tandy and Tyrone discover their abilities are two halves of the same thing: hers shows people their hopes, his shows their fears, and both are stronger when they are in contact.

nodes.title: The policeman who shot his brother
nodes.description: Tyrone Johnson's pursuit of Detective Connors, the officer who killed his brother and framed him, drives him to abandon everything else until the cover-up is finally exposed.

nodes.title: The company buried it
nodes.description: Roxxon's negligence caused the rig explosion, and the company and a sitting senator spend years burying the evidence and the people who look for it.

nodes.title: They leave together
nodes.description: With Andre defeated and the cover-up exposed, Tandy and Tyrone leave New Orleans together to find other people like them.

nodes.title: They send Stark to ruin the meeting
nodes.description: The World Security Council wants Emil Blonsky released to join the Avengers Initiative, blaming Harlem on Bruce Banner; Nick Fury refuses, so Coulson and Sitwell send Tony Stark to sabotage the meeting with Thaddeus Ross.

nodes.title: A couple with a Chitauri gun
nodes.description: A recovered Chitauri weapon left behind after the Battle of New York is used by a young couple to rob banks, and S.H.I.E.L.D. recruits rather than arrests them.

nodes.title: The real Mandarin is not amused
nodes.description: A documentary filmmaker interviewing the imprisoned Trevor Slattery reveals himself as a member of the actual Ten Rings, and breaks Slattery out to face the real Mandarin, whose name he has been wearing.

nodes.title: She takes the call herself
nodes.description: A year after the war, Peggy Carter is sidelined at the SSR until she runs an operation alone and is put in charge of the new S.H.I.E.L.D. by Howard Stark.

nodes.title: A hunt to decide who leads
nodes.description: After Ulysses Bloodstone's death, his widow Verussa summons five monster hunters to compete in a lethal hunt at Bloodstone Manor for the right to wield the Bloodstone.

nodes.title: The hunter is one of them
nodes.description: The Bloodstone reacts violently to Jack Russell's touch, exposing him as a monster; Verussa uses it to force his transformation into a werewolf.

nodes.title: She inherits what she rejected
nodes.description: Elsa Bloodstone, estranged from her father's monster-hunting legacy, kills the remaining hunters, spares the werewolf and takes possession of the manor and the Bloodstone.

nodes.title: They buy the severed head
nodes.film: The Guardians of the Galaxy Holiday Special (2022)
nodes.description: The Guardians purchase Knowhere from the Collector as a home and take in Cosmo the Spacedog, settling somewhere for the first time.

nodes.title: They kidnap Kevin Bacon
nodes.film: The Guardians of the Galaxy Holiday Special (2022)
nodes.description: Trying to cheer up a grieving Peter Quill, Mantis and Drax travel to Earth and abduct the actor Kevin Bacon, believing him to be a real hero.

nodes.title: She finally tells him
nodes.film: The Guardians of the Galaxy Holiday Special (2022)
nodes.description: Mantis tells Peter Quill that she is his half-sister, a truth she withheld for years rather than remind him of what their father Ego did.

nodes.title: The children of a serial killer
nodes.description: Daimon and Ana Helstrom, the children of a Satanist serial killer and a demonically possessed mother, use their inherited abilities to hunt the worst of humanity while barely speaking to each other.

nodes.title: Their mother is not alone in there
nodes.description: Victoria Helstrom is held in a psychiatric hospital, possessed by a demon called Mother, and her children are drawn back together by what she starts drawing on the walls.

nodes.title: She signs because of what she is
nodes.description: Elena Rodriguez is compelled to sign the Sokovia Accords because she is an Inhuman, while pursuing a private vendetta S.H.I.E.L.D. would never authorise.
